flows.name: One chat turn
flows.what: One owner message in the web UI, through the model and its tools, until every step is in durable history.

steps.name: Owner sends a message
steps.what: The owner types in an open chat; the browser posts the message detached and keeps following the chat's live feed, which carries everything the turn emits.
steps.in: message text typed in an open chat
steps.out: 202 started · the turn runs in its own goroutine

files.note: The chat's live feed and the followed approver
The chat store that sends and follows

children.name: Follow the chat feed
children.what: Every open tab already streams the chat's feed: first a replay of the running turn's frames, then each new frame as it is published.
children.out: SSE: feed_state, delta, tool_call, approval_request, turn_done…

children.name: Post the message
children.what: The chat store posts the text with detach: true, so the request returns at once and the answer arrives on the feed instead.

children.name: Cross-site guard
children.what: Rejects anything that is not JSON, comes from a non-loopback Origin or names a non-loopback Host, so a forged browser request cannot start a turn (bash runs ungated).

flags.text: POST /api/chat (handleChat) and POST /api/approve (handleApprove) decode their bodies with json.NewDecoder(r.Body) directly: no size limit and unknown fields accepted, unlike the management routes, which use decodeManagementJSONUpTo.

children.name: Pick the chat, claim the turn
children.what: Finds the open chat the request names and registers this turn; a closed chat, a held chat, a changed model or a second send get a 409.

highlight: Chat model changed; refresh before sending

children.name: Answer 202, run detached
children.what: Answers 202 started immediately and runs the turn in a goroutine with the followed approver, so closing the tab does not stop the turn.

children.name: Hand the turn to the agent
children.what: Calls the chat agent's Session.Send; a panic ends only this turn, and a busy or lease-conflict refusal is reported on the feed.

steps.name: Pin scope, preset and tools
steps.what: When the chat opens, its Workspace's Agent Preset resolves into one immutable Toolset and a Composition Receipt stored with the session; each turn then takes the session's turn lease before it writes anything.
steps.in: Workspace + revision (at chat open), then the owner message
steps.out: agent.Session (pinned Toolset, ScopeContext) holding a fenced turn lease

children.name: Open the chat
children.what: Opening a new chat in a Workspace reads the Workspace's default Agent Preset for its current revision.

children.name: Resolve the Agent Preset
children.what: Resolves each required and optional Capability of the preset against ready plugins and adds them to the base tools, producing a Toolset and its Composition Receipt.

flags.text: ADR 0012 and the plugins spec describe user-authored presets versioned in procedural Git; ResolvePresetContext knows only the four built-ins (Standard, Research, Explore, Build) and refuses any other preset ID.
A ready plugin's capabilities reach a session only when its Agent Preset names them (resolvePreset).

children.name: Store session + receipt
children.what: Creates the Workspace session and its Composition Receipt together, after checking the preset is allowed in that Workspace revision.

children.name: Build the agent
children.what: serve builds each chat's agent.Session with the resolved Toolset, the session's ScopeContext, a history and a turn owner bound to a fresh holder ID, and the background pass as its compaction flush.

flags.text: Disabling a plugin later leaves this session's Toolset intact, because a Toolset copies its tool definitions; whether those tools still work is up to the provider's Stop.

children.name: Take the turn lease
children.what: Send takes the session's turn lease, so only one turn (or one background commit) writes to the conversation at a time, and starts a heartbeat that renews it.

flags.text: A lost lease cancels the turn with ErrLeaseLost (startHeartbeat), and every append is fenced by the lease token, so a turn that lost its lease cannot write.

children.name: Append the owner message
children.what: The owner's text becomes the turn's root event; every later event of the turn hangs off it.

steps.name: Assemble the context
steps.what: Rebuilds the model request from durable state every time: stored history, repository instructions, the standing memory block, Automatic Recall evidence and the pinned tool schemas, compacting first when it would not fit.
steps.out: ChatRequest (messages + tool schemas) + context_snapshot event

children.name: Reload durable history
children.what: Loads the stored events (on later iterations only those after the last one loaded) and validates the compaction chain, so each request reflects exactly what is stored.
children.in: session ID, events loaded so far

flags.text: A tool call cut off by cancellation or a lost lease leaves a tool_intent with no outcome; history reconstruction drops such incomplete tool-call groups (incompleteToolGroupEvents) instead of replaying them.

children.name: Repository instructions
children.what: Captures once per turn the instructions file the owner enabled for the Workspace's folder and renders it as a JSON note; a folder that changed meanwhile fails the turn.

highlight: Workspace folder changed while preparing instructions

children.name: Standing memory block
children.what: Reads the accepted always-apply memories for every request, so an approval earlier in the turn already applies to its next request.

flags.text: The standing budget counts only what the approving session sees, so a later conversation can render slightly over 500 tokens; nothing is ever truncated.

children.name: Automatic Recall
children.what: At the turn's first request, searches accepted memories and earlier conversations of the same Context Scope (two results each), plus up to two more accepted-memory searches for IDs or tokens like task-12 in the message (two each), so it holds up to six accepted-memory results and two conversation excerpts as framed evidence. The Memory flow shows how.

triggers.when: at the first model request of each turn

children.name: Compact if too big
children.what: When the request would overflow the model's window, a summarizing model call replaces older events with a stored compaction summary; a provider context-length rejection gets exactly one compact-and-retry per turn.

triggers.when: a committed compaction wakes the background memory pass

children.what: POSTs the Chat Completions request with stream: true and reads the data: lines; any line, keepalives included, counts as liveness.

flags.text: A stream that goes five minutes without any line is cancelled by the idle watchdog; there is no total timeout, so long healthy streams run as long as they need.

children.name: Deltas to the feed
children.what: Each reasoning and content fragment is published on the chat's feed; the feed keeps the frames so a tab that rejoins replays them.

children.name: Retry before output
children.what: A provider failure is retried with backoff only when no text has reached the feed yet; afterwards it ends the turn.

children.name: Commit the answer
children.what: Validates the response (no choices, or finish_reason length or error, fails the turn) and appends it as an assistant_message; with no tool calls this is the turn's durable success.

flags.text: A committed final assistant message wins over a cancellation that arrived while its append was in flight: the turn still ends as a success.

steps.name: Run the tool calls
steps.what: Each tool call is recorded as an intent, run through the session's pinned Toolset (pausing for the owner when the tool is gated), and its bounded result is stored; then the turn assembles the next request.
steps.out: tool_intent, approval?, tool outcome events

children.name: Record the intent
children.what: Appends a tool_intent event with a fresh execution ID and emits tool_call to the feed before anything runs.

children.name: Find the tool and its gate
children.what: Looks the call up in the pinned Toolset; it is gated when the tool needs approval or its RequiresApproval check says so, and an erroring check counts as yes.

flags.text: bash is deliberately ungated, with no approval and no path denylist, because a shell walks around any fence; the cross-site guard exists for that reason.

children.name: Approval handshake
children.what: For a gated call the turn pauses inside Send while the owner's answer arrives as a separate HTTP request; the decision is stored before the tool may run.

flags.text: Approval ids are no secret from local software. guard only checks for JSON, a loopback Origin and a loopback Host, so any local process passes it (the CLI's connection commands rely on that); /api/chats/follow replays the running turn's frames to such a caller, approval_request ids included (chatFeed.publish keeps every frame and follow returns them); and POST /api/approve needs nothing but that id. A local process can therefore answer a gated call. Sources: Server.guard, connectionCommands.post, Server.handleFollow, sseEvents.ApprovalRequest.

children.name: Prepare and preview
children.what: Builds the effect before asking: for edit_file, a full before-and-after preview; the turn's lease is checked first, since deciding may reach a server.

children.name: Ask on the feed
children.what: Registers a pending approval under a random 8-byte id tagged with its chat, and publishes approval_request with the tool, arguments and preview on the chat's feed.

children.name: Owner answers
children.what: The tab shows the approval card; Approve or Decline posts the id and the answer.

children.name: Claim exactly once
children.what: claimPending removes the entry under the lock, so exactly one answer wins; a late or unknown id gets 404.

children.name: Wait or expire
children.what: The approver waits for the answer; with no tab following for two minutes, or when the turn stops, it expires and the model is told the owner never saw it.

children.name: Store the decision
children.what: Appends the approval event (plus a semantic approval when the tool bound a memory proposal) before the tool may run.

flags.text: A prepared tool with semantic ApprovalMetadata fails unless an approval observer is wired, so a semantic change never runs without a durable approval record.

children.name: Run it
children.what: Re-checks the lease, then runs the prepared effect or the tool itself; a decline or expiry becomes a fixed message to the model instead.
children.out: tool text, or an error result

triggers.when: the model calls delegate_research, delegate_explore or delegate_build

children.name: Store the bounded result
children.what: Bounds the result (100 KiB for most tools), appends it under the intent or the approval as succeeded, failed or cancelled, and emits tool_result to the feed.

flows.name: Workflows
flows.what: An approved workflow from its activation and schedule ticks to a run that advances node by node and records each effect's Effect Receipt.
flows.trigger: The owner approves a definition that declares a schedule, and every schedule tick (15 s by default, the first at startup) decides its due slots; runs also start from the web (POST /api/workflows/start), the CLI (evie workflows run) and a chat's workflow_start tool.

steps.name: Approve and activate
steps.what: The owner approves exactly the proposal card they reviewed, and the store records it as the next active version, with its schedule, in one transaction.

Added the Architecture and History tabs: the explorer's components, containers, sequence flows and diagrams moved into the map as parts, edges and sequences, and History reads CHANGELOG.md; the explorer viewer retired, so the snapshot holds only this page
Corrected the map: the background pass is off unless EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on with OPENROUTER_API_KEY or EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG enables it, and Automatic Recall also runs up to two exact-selector searches
Map created: Evie's System view drawn as flows, from the approved prototype

summary.text: The one person Evie works for: Evie has no user accounts, and its web server binds only to loopback because it has no authentication.

does.text: Chats with Evie in the web UI, where the browser posts each message and reads the turn's events back as a stream.
Chats in the terminal REPL that `evie` with no arguments starts, answering each gated tool call at an `approve? [y/N]` prompt.
Runs one-shot commands: `evie` management subcommands, `todo` for Task Trees, `finance` for banks and transactions, and `ytscribe` for YouTube transcripts.
Grants Action Approval for consequential tool calls; the web route for it accepts only JSON requests whose Origin and Host are loopback, so a foreign web page cannot forge an approval.
Signs in to outside accounts in the browser: MCP servers through an OAuth flow that Evie starts, and banks through Plaid's hosted Link page.
Reviews what background work proposes, such as the background memory pass's memory proposals, before anything is accepted.

owns.text: Supplies the credentials and switches Evie reads at startup, from the shell environment or `~/.evie/.env`, such as OPENROUTER_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN.

gotchas.text: There is no login: anything that can reach the loopback port acts as the owner, which is why a non-loopback `EVIE_ADDR` is refused outright rather than warned about.

summary.text: A Go-native personal agent runtime with local SQLite persistence, purpose-built tools, an OpenRouter conversational client, and a web interface.

does.text: Runs a model-and-tools loop for each chat, calling OpenRouter for every model turn and running the tools its session's Agent Preset composes.

Composes ten compiled First-party Plugins (Web, Finance, YouTube, Todo, Memory, Subagents, Workflows, GitHub, MCP and Workspace tabs) through the Plugin Manager; each defaults to enabled and the owner's choice is durable.
Keeps durable state on the owner's machine in three SQLite databases (Evie, finance and the YouTube library) and a bare procedural Git repository.

Runs background hosts inside its long-lived processes: the workflow scheduler, the background memory pass, retrieval index maintenance, the optional memory compiler, subagent recovery and, in `evie serve` only, GitHub change sync.

Reaches outside systems only through purpose-built clients: OpenRouter, a local Ollama, hosted MCP servers, GitHub, Plaid, YouTube, Brave Search, web pages, the local Codex app-server, launchd and the owner's login shell.

owns.text: Conversations, memory, Tasks, Workspaces, Workflow Runs, plugin state and MCP connection records in the Evie database at `~/.evie/evie.db`.
Linked banks and transactions in `~/.finance/finance.db`, and the transcript library in `~/.evie/transcripts/transcripts.db`.
Reviewed Workflow Definitions in the procedural Git repository at `~/.evie/procedural`, and MCP credentials in the macOS Keychain.

interfaces.text: A loopback web UI and API served by `evie serve` at `EVIE_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:6687`).
Four command-line binaries: `evie` (REPL, `serve`, `cron-exec` and management subcommands), `todo`, `finance` and `ytscribe`.

gotchas.text: Third-party text (web pages, search snippets, YouTube transcripts and MCP results) reaches the model only framed as untrusted data, never as instructions.
Several pieces assume macOS: launchd fires cron jobs, `/usr/bin/security` reaches the Keychain, the folder picker runs `osascript`, and the build-worker sandbox is Seatbelt (bubblewrap on Linux).

summary.text: The hosted model router Evie calls for every remote model: chat turns, compaction, subagent workers, the background memory pass, and workflow AI and agent steps.

does.text: Receives chat turns as streamed Chat Completions at `/api/v1/chat/completions`, or at `/api/v1/responses` for the one model Evie sends through the Responses API, GPT-6 Astra.
Answers model metadata: the `/models` catalog for chat selection and prices, and per-model and per-endpoint limits that size each chat's context window.
Is called from serve, the REPL, the background memory pass, the workflow scheduler and a foreground `evie workflows run`, always with OPENROUTER_API_KEY as a bearer token.

gotchas.text: Its error bodies are treated as untrusted: Evie drains a bounded prefix and keeps only the status, a Retry-After hint and whether the body reported a context-length rejection.

The default chat model is `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (EVIE_MODEL overrides it); when metadata discovery fails, only it and `moonshotai/kimi-k3` fall back to a checked-in window, and every other model fails to start.
Background work sends data here only on opt-in: the background memory pass needs EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on, and workflow AI and agent steps need EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS=on.

summary.text: A local Ollama server on a loopback address, which Evie uses for memory embeddings and for the pinned local extractor, so memory text sent to it stays on the machine.

does.text: Embeds memory text with the pinned `all-minilm:22m` model at `/api/embed`, after checking the model's manifest digest at `/api/tags`, when EVIE_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT is set and EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on.

Runs the pinned extraction model for the memory compiler at `/api/generate` and for the local background memory pass at `/api/chat`, after verifying the runtime version, model digest, template and tokenizer through `/api/version`, `/api/tags` and `/api/show`.

gotchas.text: The two clients accept different endpoints: embeddings take loopback HTTP or a `unix:/absolute/socket` path, while the extractor takes only loopback HTTP with an explicit port.
Neither client uses a proxy or follows redirects, so a misconfigured endpoint cannot carry memory text elsewhere.
Evie never downloads models: the owner installs the pinned model, and a missing model or a changed digest fails the request instead.

summary.text: Hosted MCP servers at https URLs, reached over Streamable HTTP, which the owner connects through an OAuth sign-in that serve runs; their reviewed tools reach web chats.

does.text: Sign-in: serve discovers the server's protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, registers a client dynamically when needed, and runs PKCE S256 with the browser returning to serve's own callback route.
Tool use: serve keeps at most one live MCP session per connection, opened on first use with no client capabilities, and lists and calls tools on it.
Tokens: serve's transport adds the bearer token only over https to the connection's own host, and re-sends a request once only after a 401 that a token refresh answered.

gotchas.text: Server text is untrusted: tool descriptions, schemas and results reach the model only as framed tool-result data, never as tool definitions or instructions.
Evie does not follow an MCP redirect, because following one would re-send a POST.
MCP tools run only in serve's chats, and Workflow Definitions cannot reference them.

summary.text: GitHub, reached through its REST API with a fine-grained token from GITHUB_TOKEN, and through git over HTTPS for pushes, fetches and clones.

does.text: Answers REST calls for the token's user, repositories (read and create), pull requests (list, read, open, merge, close), Actions workflow runs and combined commit statuses.
Receives git push, fetch and clone from the Workspace folder, with the token sent per command as an extra HTTP header for `https://github.com/`.
Is synced by serve every 60 seconds, and written to by the owner's pushes and merges (web UI or `evie changes`) and by workflows' GitHub steps.

gotchas.text: Without GITHUB_TOKEN, GitHub is simply not connected: Repositories stay local and the change sync has nothing to do.
The token never goes into a URL, git config, remote, log, returned error or worker sandbox, and git's output is scrubbed of it.
GitHub's Checks API does not accept fine-grained tokens, so a Repository's checks are its Actions workflow runs and commit statuses, and services that report only check runs are not seen.
Each REST request times out after ten seconds; a remote git command after five minutes.

summary.text: Plaid's production environment, through which the finance domain links banks and syncs their transactions.

does.text: Hosts bank linking: Evie creates a hosted Link session whose URL must be on `https://secure.plaid.com`, the owner finishes consent in the browser, and Evie completes the link and saves the new Item.
Returns added, modified and removed transactions for each linked Item from its stored sync cursor.
Is called by the `finance` CLI, by serve's Spending page and finance tools, and by the finance workflow's ledger-sync effect.

gotchas.text: The environment is hard-coded to production; there is no sandbox mode.
Plaid access tokens are stored in the finance database's `items` table, not in a secret store.
Plaid's machine-readable error codes drive recovery, such as restarting a sync after the data changed during pagination.

summary.text: YouTube's website and internal player and browse endpoints, from which the transcript library fetches captions and channel video lists.

does.text: Serves watch pages, the `youtubei/v1/player` endpoint that Evie calls as the Android app client to find caption tracks, and the caption files themselves.
Serves channel video lists through channel pages and the `youtubei/v1/browse` endpoint for `ytscribe scrape`.

gotchas.text: Fetching depends on YouTube's internal API and an Android client identity pinned to one app version, so a YouTube change can break it with no change in Evie.
A redirect to YouTube's consent page stops the fetch, and caption URLs must be https on a youtube.com host.
Terminal outcomes such as a video without captions are cached and reused until a fetch asks for a refresh.

summary.text: Brave's web search API, which the Web plugin's `web_search` tool queries with BRAVE_API_KEY.

does.text: Receives one GET per search at `api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search` with the query and a result count from 1 to 20, authenticated by the X-Subscription-Token header.
Returns titles, URLs and snippets, which Evie frames as untrusted third-party text before the model sees them.

gotchas.text: A search times out after 15 seconds, and a response over 1 MB is refused rather than parsed.
The tool's description tells the model the free tier allows one request per second, and a 429 comes back as an instruction to wait and retry.

summary.text: Any http or https page the Web plugin's `web_fetch` tool reads for the model, including local and private-network addresses for the main chat.

does.text: Is fetched one URL per call, with http upgraded to https except for local and private hosts, credentials in the URL stripped, and non-text content or pages over 10 MB refused.
Is converted from HTML to Markdown and framed as untrusted data; text past 100 KB is trimmed and saved to a file.
Redirects on the same host are followed; a redirect to another host is returned to the model as a new URL to fetch again.

gotchas.text: The main chat may fetch localhost and private-network addresses on purpose, but delegated research workers may dial only public addresses, judged after DNS resolution on every connection.
There is no JavaScript rendering, so a single-page app returns an error suggesting the page is rendered by JavaScript.

summary.text: The owner's local Codex installation, whose app-server and session logs serve reads to show Codex account and token usage in Data > Usage.

does.text: Runs as `codex app-server --stdio` once per configured Codex home, with MCP servers, analytics and apps turned off, answering only allowlisted account reads within 20 seconds.
Provides token metadata from the `sessions` and `archived_sessions` JSONL files in each Codex home, which Evie indexes in memory by file offset without copying text.
Is found through EVIE_CODEX_BIN, the ChatGPT desktop bundle or PATH, with homes from EVIE_CODEX_HOMES (at most four absolute paths), CODEX_HOME or `~/.codex`.

gotchas.text: It is read only when Data > Usage asks: the account at most once a minute, and the local index every 30 seconds, or every 3 seconds until a first full scan completes.
Its errors, stderr, reset credits and credentials are never forwarded, and an unavailable Codex shows as stale or unavailable without hiding Evie's own usage.
An invalid EVIE_CODEX_HOMES stops `evie serve` at startup.

summary.text: macOS's launchd, which fires the owner's cron jobs by starting `evie cron-exec <job-id>` on each job's calendar schedule, whether or not Evie is running.

does.text: Loads the plist `cron_add` writes to `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.evie.cron.<name>.plist`, with StartCalendarInterval entries translated from the cron expression, after a launchctl bootout and bootstrap.
Unloads a job when `cron_remove` boots it out and deletes its plist; `cron_list` reads jobs from the Evie database and never asks launchd.
Runs a fire missed during sleep on wake, coalescing several misses into one run; fires missed while the machine was off are lost.

gotchas.text: The plist records the `evie` binary's path at the time of `cron_add`, so jobs must be removed and added again if the binary moves.
The Evie database is the source of truth and plists are generated, so drift such as a hand-deleted plist goes unnoticed.
Cron jobs are a separate, older mechanism from Workflow Schedules: launchd fires a raw shell command, outside the Workflow Runtime and its leases.

summary.text: The owner's own login shell (`$SHELL`), which runs the model's bash commands, cron job commands and the web terminal on the owner's machine.

does.text: Runs each bash tool command as `$SHELL -l -c` with the owner's shell snapshot sourced, keeping the working directory between calls, with a two-minute default timeout that can rise to ten minutes.
Runs cron job commands the same way from the home directory, bounded at 30 minutes per run.
Runs as an interactive login shell on a PTY in the Workspace folder for the web terminal.

Runs build workers' bash only inside an OS sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) with no network and writes confined to the worktree and its private temp folder; without a sandbox, build workers get no bash.

gotchas.text: The main chat's bash is ungated, with no approval prompt and no path denylist, because a shell walks around any fence; the defense is that the owner reads what Evie does.
The main chat's bash and the web terminal inherit Evie's whole environment, including keys loaded from `~/.evie/.env`; only build workers' sandboxed bash gets a built environment without them.

summary.text: The `evie serve` process: the loopback web server and the runtime behind it, which also runs Evie's background hosts while it is up.

does.text: Listens on EVIE_ADDR, by default `127.0.0.1:6687`, and refuses any address that is not loopback.
Serves the React build compiled into the binary and the `/api` routes, streaming each chat turn's events back to the browser.
Runs each open chat's agent session against OpenRouter, resolving the selected model's context profile per chat and composing tools from the chat's Agent Preset.
Starts the workflow scheduler, subagent recovery, retrieval index maintenance, the background memory pass, the optional memory compiler host and, with GITHUB_TOKEN, the 60-second GitHub change sync.
Is the only process that holds MCP tokens: it runs OAuth sign-ins, refreshes tokens, keeps one live session per MCP connection and answers the CLI's connection commands.
Hosts the owner's Workspace surfaces: files, diffs and tabs from the attached folder, a terminal, Changes with push and merge, Spending through Plaid, Data > Usage from Codex, and memory review.
Shuts down on SIGINT or SIGTERM: the HTTP server gets five seconds to drain, and each background host up to five seconds to stop.

owns.text: Only per-process state: open chats and their live feeds, pending approvals, MCP sessions and terminals; everything durable is written to the databases.

interfaces.text: Loopback HTTP: `/api` JSON routes, most of them POST-only management routes behind the same guard; outside it, the System page under `/explorer/` and each Workspace tab's sealed pages under `/workspace-tabs/`; and the static app for every other path.
The OAuth callback for MCP sign-ins at `/api/connections/oauth/callback` on serve's own address.

gotchas.text: If the default Agent Preset is invalid, serve still starts, but as a management-only server with no chat, while the memory hosts and the workflow scheduler run anyway.
A workflow runtime configuration error stops serve at startup, whereas the REPL logs `workflow scheduler off` and keeps chatting.
Once the preset is valid, a missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY stops serve, because the chat client is built at startup.
Running serve and the REPL together runs two workflow schedulers and two background memory passes on one database; leases stored there keep them from doing the same work twice.

summary.text: The interactive terminal REPL that `evie` with no command starts: one chat at a time, plus the background hosts a long-lived Evie process runs.

does.text: Shows a numbered chooser of resumable sessions, registered projects and Workspaces, a new Global session, and registering the launch directory as a project; the choice sets the session's Context Scope.
Streams each reply to the terminal and pauses gated tool calls at an `approve? [y/N]` prompt.
Answers `/memory` commands typed into the chat, which inspect Semantic Memory or replay accepted operations into a shadow projection, without a model call and never as model capabilities.
Runs the workflow scheduler, subagent recovery, retrieval index maintenance, the background memory pass and the optional compiler host, like serve, but no GitHub change sync.
Closes standard input when SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives, so a blocked read ends and the hosts stop.

gotchas.text: MCP tools are unavailable in REPL chats: they answer that MCP tools run only in `evie serve` chats.
Failing to resolve the default Agent Preset, or a missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY, stops the REPL when it builds the session.
A workflow runtime configuration problem only turns the scheduler off with a reason; chat still starts.

summary.text: One-shot `evie` subcommands that inspect or manage Evie's state and then exit.

does.text: Dispatches on the first argument through a chain of handlers: `workflows` review (validate, simulate, templates) needs no database, `connections` and `workspaces mcp-tools` only call serve, and every other command opens the Evie database first.
Offers memory commands: `memory-health`, `memory-backfill`, `memory-compiler` (status and disable), `memory-compile` and `memory-candidates`, `memory-review`, and `memory-background status`.
Offers Workspace and code commands: `workspaces`, `projects`, `worktrees` (list and clean) and `changes` (list, push, merge, disarm and close).

Runs `workflows` activation commands (propose, approve, run, inspect, schedules and more) on a Workflow Runtime and subagent supervisor of its own; `workflows run` without `--detach` executes the run in this process until it finishes or pauses.
Runs `plugins`, `presets` and `sessions` through the same Plugin Manager the chat uses, to manage plugin enablement and inspect Agent Presets and sessions.
Runs `memory-compile` against one owner-selected range with the pinned local extractor named by `--config`, in this process.
Runs the owner's merge gate for `changes merge` and `close` in this process with its own subagent supervisor; serve's recovery leaves those steps alone while they run.

gotchas.text: The usage line printed for an unknown command lists only `serve`, `cron-exec`, `plugins`, `presets`, `sessions` and `workflows`, though many more subcommands exist.
Opening the Evie database applies its schema upgrades, so any database-backed command migrates `~/.evie/evie.db` to the binary's version.

Before `plugins`, `presets` and `sessions` run, startup imports the legacy Todo list, recovers inactive Task Claims and subagent records, and applies plugin defaults, so even these inspection commands write to the database.

`connections` and `workspaces mcp-tools` are clients of serve's routes, because only serve holds MCP tokens: when the connection to serve is refused they fail with 'evie serve is not running at <addr>', and any other failure to reach it is returned as it is.

summary.text: The one-shot `evie cron-exec <job-id>` process that launchd starts on a cron job's schedule: it runs the job's command and records the run.

does.text: Reads the job's command from the `jobs` table, runs it with `tools.RunScheduled` in the owner's login shell from the home directory, and appends the output and exit code to `job_runs`.
Bounds each run at 30 minutes and caps the output it stores.
Exits 0 even when the job fails, so launchd does not treat Evie as broken; it exits 2 for bad arguments and 1 for an unusable job or database.

gotchas.text: It never builds a model client, so it runs headless under launchd without an API key.
A plist whose job row was deleted fails with a message that its plist is stale and should be removed and added again.

summary.text: The React single-page app the owner uses in a browser, built with Vite and compiled into the `evie` binary.

does.text: Is served by `evie serve` from the embedded `ui/dist` build, with fingerprinted assets cached forever and `index.html` never cached.
Sends each chat message as a JSON POST to `/api/chat` and parses the reply's `event:` and `data:` blocks from the fetch body, because EventSource cannot POST.
Offers the chat with model selection, Workspaces with files, a terminal and tabs, data views, memory review and notifications.

interfaces.text: Talks only to serve's loopback origin, sending the exact `application/json` content type the server's guard requires.

gotchas.text: The build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone must run `npm --prefix internal/web/ui run build` before `go build`, and the embed fails naming the missing directory.
Unknown paths return the app shell rather than a 404.

summary.text: Evie's main SQLite database at `~/.evie/evie.db`, shared by every `evie` process and `todo`: conversations, memory, Tasks, Workspaces, Workflow Runs, plugin state and more.

does.text: Opens through eviedb, which creates `~/.evie` with mode 0700, forces the file to mode 0600, and applies the whole schema and its in-place upgrades on every open.
Runs in WAL mode with foreign keys on and a five-second busy timeout on every pooled connection.
Can be open in several processes at once: serve, the REPL, management commands, cron-exec and `todo`, with the cron tools opening it again for their own job rows.

owns.text: Conversation history, which is Episodic Memory, plus Semantic Memory, Memory Candidates and the derived full-text and dense retrieval indexes.
Task Trees and their claims, Workspaces with their folders and presets, Workflow Runs, cron jobs and their runs.
MCP connection records, which never carry credentials.

gotchas.text: Every process that opens it runs the schema upgrades, so a newer binary migrates the file the moment any command touches it, even `todo list`.
The read-only open skips the schema and fails if the file does not exist yet.

summary.text: The finance domain's SQLite database at `~/.finance/finance.db`, which holds linked banks, transactions and their categorization, including Plaid access tokens.

does.text: Opens through finance, which creates `~/.finance` with mode 0700, forces the file to mode 0600 because access tokens live in it, and applies an idempotent CREATE IF NOT EXISTS schema on every open.
Is written by the `finance` CLI, by serve's Spending page and the finance tools, and by the finance workflow effects that sync and categorize the ledger.

owns.text: Plaid Items with their access tokens and sync cursors, transactions, categories, merchant and name rules, Budget Entries and limits, review decisions and effect receipts.
Linked accounts, account snapshots and the hosted Link sessions of bank linking.

gotchas.text: Unlike the Evie database it does not switch to WAL, so it uses SQLite's default rollback journal and each connection waits up to five seconds for a lock.
Holding Plaid access tokens in SQLite departs from ADR 0028, which gives credentials to the Kernel's secret storage.

summary.text: The YouTube transcript library's SQLite database at `~/.evie/transcripts/transcripts.db`.

does.text: Opens through youtube, which creates and locks down its folder to mode 0700, forces the file to 0600, and applies an idempotent schema on every open.
Is written by `ytscribe` and the YouTube plugin's transcript tool, and read through a read-only open by the database query tool.

owns.text: Channels, videos, transcripts with their fetch states, and a full-text index over transcripts.

gotchas.text: Like the finance database it does not switch to WAL, unlike the Evie database.

summary.text: Evie's procedural Git repository at `~/.evie/procedural`: a private bare repository that is the reviewed, versioned home of Workflow Definitions.

does.text: Is created on first use as a private bare repository (mode 0700, initial branch master).
Is written only with Git plumbing and a compare-and-swap move of master, so there is no work tree to leave dirty and a crash before the ref moves leaves only unreferenced objects.
Receives Workflow Definition proposals, and each built-in workflow version when it is first resolved, from the Workflow Runtime, which reads definitions back at exact commits.
Runs every git command with hooks, fsmonitor, pagers, signing, automatic maintenance and transports off, in a built environment that ignores global and system Git configuration.

owns.text: What was proposed and approved, as committed files; approval records and Workflow Runs live in the Evie database.

gotchas.text: It sits inside `~/.evie`, which every file tool, explore root and sandboxed shell refuses, so no worker can read or write it.
Readers name an exact commit, so later commits never change what an earlier commit reads.

ADR 0012 places user-authored Agent Presets here and ADR 0028 places reviewed Workspace configuration here, but today only the Workflow Runtime writes it; presets are compiled into the plugins package and Workspace presets live in the Evie database.

summary.text: The macOS login Keychain, where serve keeps each MCP connection's OAuth credentials as one generic-password item.

does.text: Is reached through `/usr/bin/security`, with service `dev.evie.mcp` and the Connection ID as the account.
Receives secrets only on standard input, base64-encoded inside a `security -i` line, never in process arguments.

owns.text: MCP access tokens, refresh tokens and client secrets, which never appear in SQLite, procedural Git, logs, tool results or model context.

gotchas.text: Credentials are capped at 3,000 bytes of JSON so one base64 line fits security(1)'s interactive line limit; larger ones fail.
Only serve touches it, so exactly one process refreshes a connection's tokens; CLI connection commands call serve instead.

ADR 0028 gives all credentials to the Kernel's secret storage, but only MCP credentials live here: API keys and GITHUB_TOKEN come from the environment or `~/.evie/.env`, and Plaid access tokens sit in the finance database.
When security(1) cannot run or fails, the store reports the Keychain as unavailable and a connection can show the `keychain_unavailable` status.

summary.text: `~/.evie/.env`, the dotenv file every `evie` command loads at startup for credentials and settings.

does.text: Is loaded first, then `.env` and `../../.env` relative to the working directory as a development convenience, each in its own call so a missing file does not stop the next.
Never overrides a variable the shell already set.

owns.text: The credentials the code reads from the environment: OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, BRAVE_API_KEY, and Plaid's PLAID_CLIENT_ID and PLAID_SECRET.
Feature settings such as EVIE_MODEL, EVIE_ADDR, EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY, EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG, EVIE_MEMORY_BACKGROUND and EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS.

gotchas.text: `web_search`'s missing-key error tells the model to add BRAVE_API_KEY to the repo-root `.env`, but an installed `evie` reads `~/.evie/.env` first and sees a repo-root `.env` only when started from the repository root or `cmd/evie`.

The `finance` command does not read this file: it calls godotenv once with `../../.env` and `.env`, and godotenv stops at the first file it cannot read, so the local `.env` its comment calls a fallback loads only when `../../.env` also exists.
Evie does not check this file's permissions, unlike its databases, which it forces to mode 0600.
Keys loaded from it reach the main chat's bash commands and the web terminal, which inherit Evie's environment; only build workers' sandboxed bash gets a built environment.

summary.text: The folder on the owner's disk attached to each Workspace, which may hold its Repository; Evie reads it, runs git and shells in it, and keeps build worktrees under its `.evie` folder.

does.text: Is listed, read and diffed by serve for the Files view, and supplies the Workspace's tabs, which serve reads from the folder.
Hosts the web terminal's interactive login shell.

Holds build workers' git worktrees at `<repo>/.evie/worktrees/<attempt>` with private temp folders at `<repo>/.evie/tmp/<attempt>`, kept out of the owner's status by the repository's local info/exclude.
Is where pushes, fetches and clones to GitHub run, with the token passed to git per command.
Is chosen by the owner in the web UI, where serve can open the macOS folder dialog through osascript.

owns.text: The owner's own files and Repository; Evie's only additions are the `.evie` build area and its exclude line.

gotchas.text: Changing a Workspace's folder is refused while a turn runs or the Workspace has unfinished Changes, and the change stops that Workspace's open terminals.
Build worktrees live inside the Workspace folder, never inside `~/.evie`, and a repository that tracks `.evie` cannot be used for build work.

summary.text: The `todo` command, the owner's CLI for durable Task Trees in the Evie database.

does.text: Lists, gets, adds, updates and changes the status of Tasks, releases Task Claims, and shows a Task Tree's orchestration progress, including dependencies, claims, build workers and what `todo_ready` would offer.
Opens `~/.evie/evie.db` directly and, before every command, imports the legacy Todo list and recovers inactive Task Claims.
Works in Global scope without `--session`; with a primary session it uses that session's Workspace or project context.

gotchas.text: Without `--session`, changes are attributed to the owner under a Global session with the fixed ID `todo-cli`, and a delegated session cannot authorize owner CLI access.
`todo delete` is deprecated: it cancels and keeps the Task.

summary.text: The `finance` command, the CLI over the finance domain: link banks through Plaid, sync transactions, seed rules and categorize.

does.text: `link` runs or resumes the durable hosted Plaid Link flow: it prints the hosted URL, waits up to 35 minutes for completion and saves the new Item.
`sync` pulls new transactions for every linked bank and prints added, modified and removed counts per bank.
`rules` seeds merchant rules from `~/.finance/merchantLookup.json` plus the built-in name patterns, and `categorize` applies rules to unreviewed transactions.

gotchas.text: `link` and `sync` need PLAID_CLIENT_ID and PLAID_SECRET and fail fast without them; the Plaid environment is always production.
Its `.env` loading differs from `evie`: one godotenv call with `../../.env` then `.env` stops at the first missing file, and `~/.evie/.env` is never read.
`finance db` prints a fixed 'tables: items, transactions' line; it only proves the database opens and its schema applies.

summary.text: The `ytscribe` command, the CLI for the YouTube transcript library.

does.text: `fetch` fetches and caches one video's transcript, `scrape` walks a channel's videos with a limit and a delay between them, and `import` loads a legacy transcript corpus from a folder.
Uses the same transcript service and HTTP client as the YouTube plugin's tool, over the same database.

gotchas.text: It needs no credentials and reads no `.env` file.

summary.text: The Workflow Runtime's background scheduler inside serve and the REPL: it executes queued Workflow Runs, fires due Workflow Schedules and recovers runs whose process died.

does.text: Polls for runnable work and runs passes in a bounded pool of worker slots (EVIE_WORKFLOW_WORKERS), waking early when the runtime signals new work.
Decides due schedule slots under a single runner lease, with the first tick at start, so every startup applies the Catch-up Policies.
Recovers runs whose process died once their leases expire, and retries after durable backoffs.
Reads approved Workflow Definitions from the procedural repository at their pinned commits and keeps run state in the Evie database.
Executes capability steps through plugins (such as the finance ledger sync and GitHub Changes), AI steps through OpenRouter, and agent steps through the Kernel subagent supervisor.

gotchas.text: AI and agent steps are off by default because they send run data to the model provider: they need EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS=on and OPENROUTER_API_KEY, a setting separate from EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY.
Stopping lets nodes in flight finish and releases leases within five seconds; a pass still inside a node keeps its lease until it expires and the next process recovers the run.
serve and the REPL each start one, and another process, such as a foreground `evie workflows run`, may claim a run first; leases in the Evie database decide who executes it.

summary.text: The background memory pass inside serve and the REPL, off unless EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on with OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG naming a local extractor: it reads owner messages and proposes memory changes for the owner to review.

does.text: Resolves its configuration from the environment at startup, and any problem disables it with a reason instead of stopping Evie.

Uses a pinned OpenRouter Chat Completions model when remote memory is allowed, otherwise the pinned loopback extractor of EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG, and reads the remote model's catalog price at start for its spend caps.
Reads only owner user messages of root conversations, never assistant, tool, web or delegated text.
Is also every root conversation's compaction flush, so a compaction offers its range to the pass.
Ticks until shutdown under a runner lease in the Evie database; shutdown cancels an in-flight model call and the durable cursor lets the next process redo the batch.

gotchas.text: It only proposes: it never writes Memory Candidates or accepted memory itself.
If the catalog price cannot be read within ten seconds, the pass uses a conservative fallback price.
`evie memory-background status` shows the same configuration and durable progress but never starts a pass or contacts a provider.

summary.text: The optional memory compiler host inside serve and the REPL, started only when EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG names a pinned local extractor configuration.

does.text: Reads the configuration file as strict, size-bounded JSON and builds the loopback Ollama extractor for its Compiler Generation.

Runs the Evie database's compiler host, whose separate selection and extraction loops turn retained Episodic Memory into Memory Candidates, so a blocked local request cannot stop new work from being found.
Logs when reconciliation starts failing and when it recovers.

gotchas.text: A bad configuration only logs 'memory compiler unavailable'; chat and explicit memory keep working.
Per-conversation compiler activation is retired: the background pass reads every conversation, and `memory-compiler` keeps only status and disable.
Shutdown waits at most five seconds for cleanup.

summary.text: A loop inside serve and the REPL that keeps memory's derived retrieval indexes caught up, independently of chat turns.

does.text: Calls RefreshMemoryIndex in batches of 256 under a five-second deadline: every second when idle, every 100 ms while work is pending, and every five seconds after a failure.
Embeds at most 16 new inputs per call through the local Ollama embedding model when dense retrieval is enabled.
Logs once when the index becomes unavailable and once when it recovers.

gotchas.text: A new or rebuilt index generation cannot serve queries until maintenance has reconciled its retained coverage, so reads report partial coverage meanwhile.

summary.text: A loop inside serve and the REPL that reconciles subagent execution records for the process's lifetime; it never starts a child or a model call.

does.text: Settles outcomes this process decided but could not record, then recovers subagent records, every 250 ms while healthy and backing off to ten seconds after failures.
Checks merge-gate steps that a crash or lost turn left in progress every ten seconds.
Runs whether or not the Subagents plugin is enabled.

gotchas.text: Startup also runs one recovery pass before the loop, and an unrecoverable record is logged and retried rather than blocking startup.

summary.text: A loop inside `evie serve` that syncs each Workspace's GitHub pull requests every 60 seconds when GITHUB_TOKEN is set.

does.text: Syncs every Workspace with a GitHub Repository at start and then every 60 seconds, refreshing each open Change's pull request state, checks and mergeability.
Hands each sync result to the owner's Merger, which fires armed merges and cleans up after merges done on GitHub.
Still answers the refresh route without a token, but has nothing to sync.

gotchas.text: Only serve starts this loop; the REPL and the CLI start none.

summary.text: A minimal client for OpenRouter's Chat Completions and Responses APIs that owns request encoding, streaming, response normalization and model metadata, and depends on nothing else in Evie.

does.text: NewClient builds the only kind of Client, rejecting an empty API key so a misconfigured environment fails at startup, and points it at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`.

ChatStream sends one streaming request and assembles the reply: content and reasoning fragments go to live callbacks as they arrive, tool-call fragments are joined by their index, and a Chat Completions stream must end with `[DONE]`.
Carries the Working Memory projection the agent assembles for each model call, as the request's messages, tools and output limit.
UsesResponses routes exactly one verified model, `openai/gpt-6-astra`, to the Responses API, and every other model keeps Chat Completions rather than guessing its capabilities.

For Responses it encodes history as input items with `store:false`, low reasoning effort by default, encrypted reasoning included and `require_parameters` set, and checks that streamed function calls agree with the final completed response before returning.
PrepareRequest freezes the exact Responses wire bytes and RequestBytes returns them, so context admission, snapshots and dispatch all measure and send the same body.

ResolveContextProfile turns a model into validated token limits: it reads the model and its endpoints from OpenRouter, takes the smallest window among eligible active routes, and applies the working ceiling, the output reserve and a 4,096-token estimation margin.
ResolveChatContextProfile does the same for a chat's selected model, but lets the default working ceiling shrink to that model's window unless EVIE_CONTEXT_WORKING_TOKENS is set.
Reuses a discovered profile for ten minutes per model and configuration, so opening a chat on a recently used model makes no request; failed lookups and fallbacks are never cached.
ListChatModels returns the catalog models a chat can actually use (text in and out, tool support, an output limit that fits Evie's reply reserve, no variants or routers), sorted by author and name.
ModelPricing reads one model's per-token prompt and completion prices from the catalog, which the background memory pass and workflow model steps use for their spend caps.

Serves workflow AI steps through the Workflow Runtime's adapter, which sends exactly two messages, asks for a JSON object and sends no tools, and agent steps through the subagent supervisor configured with the same kind of client.
Normalizes token usage from both protocols into one TokenUsage, keeping a missing counter distinct from a reported zero.
Encodes prompt-cache breakpoints as `cache_control` content parts for models that OpenRouter caches only at explicit markers, which UsesExplicitCacheBreakpoints names as Anthropic and Qwen models.
WithWorkerLimits and WithOutputLimit derive narrower profiles for subagent workers and bounded calls, never raising the parent's limits.

owns.text: No durable data: each Client holds only its API key, its HTTP client and an in-memory cache of context profiles.
The shared conversation wire types that the agent and its callers exchange: Message, ToolCall, Tool, ChatRequest, ChatResponse and TokenUsage.
The model ids it knows by name: the built-in Kimi model and the default DeepSeek model, which have checked-in fallback windows, and Astra, which uses Responses.

interfaces.text: Client methods: ChatStream (used by every production caller), Chat (non-streaming, called only by tests), ResolveContextProfile, ResolveChatContextProfile, ListChatModels and ModelPricing.
Consumers own the narrow interfaces they need over it: agent.Client, memorybackground.ChatClient and workflowruntime.OpenRouterClient.

StreamError is the failure contract: a stable Kind (provider_error or provider_response_invalid), the HTTP status, a clamped Retry-After, NoResponse for failures before any status, and ContextLengthExceeded.
PrepareRequest, RequestBytes, ResponseRequestPartSizes and UsesResponses let callers account for the exact bytes they will send.

It reads three settings itself: EVIE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS (an explicit hard window that skips discovery), EVIE_CONTEXT_WORKING_TOKENS (default 262,144) and EVIE_CONTEXT_OUTPUT_RESERVE_TOKENS (default 16,384).

gotchas.text: A stream that goes five minutes without any line, keepalive comments included, is cancelled by an idle watchdog; there is no total timeout, so long healthy streams run as long as they need.
Only a failure before any HTTP status that is neither a timeout nor a cancellation is marked NoResponse, because only that proves nothing was generated and the call may be retried.
Provider error bodies are untrusted and may echo credentials, so at most 64 KiB is drained and only scanned for a context-length marker, and the body is never kept.
A Chat Completions stream that stops at `finish_reason: length` is an error, so truncated text or tool arguments never look complete, and `finish_reason: error` mid-stream fails too.

When metadata discovery fails, only `moonshotai/kimi-k3` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` fall back to a checked-in 262,144-token window, with a startup warning; every other model, Astra included, fails.
Astra rejects a temperature and accepts only low, medium, high, xhigh or max reasoning effort, and the background memory pass and workflow model steps refuse Responses models outright.
Responses output items, including encrypted reasoning, live on Message.ResponseItems only for the active tool loop and are never serialized as Chat messages or evidence.
Client.Chat takes no context, so it cannot be cancelled; no production code calls it.

The HTTP client clones Go's default transport with bounded dial, TLS and header timeouts, unless an instrumented process replaced that transport, in which case it routes through the replacement unchanged.
Responses bodies and streams are capped at 16 MiB and must be valid UTF-8; model metadata is capped at 1 MiB per lookup and 8 MiB for the catalog.
A message with blank text cannot carry a cache breakpoint, because providers reject empty text blocks.

summary.text: Implements the one selected local-only embedding protocol: Ollama's pinned `all-minilm:22m` model at a loopback or Unix-socket endpoint, verified by manifest digest, producing normalized 384-value vectors for memory retrieval.

does.text: New accepts only plain loopback HTTP with a literal IP address (no host name, credentials, query, fragment or path beyond `/`) or an absolute `unix:` socket path, and builds a transport that dials only that address, uses no proxy and refuses redirects.
Embed sends one batch of 1 to 16 non-empty UTF-8 inputs of at most 1,024 bytes each to `/api/embed`, with truncation off, a 30-second keep-alive and four threads.
It checks the model's manifest digest at `/api/tags` before and after inference, so a re-tagged model cannot silently replace the selected generation mid-batch.
It validates the reply (same model, one vector per input, 384 finite values, non-zero magnitude) and returns unit-length float32 vectors.
Every call is bounded: one ten-second deadline covers both manifest reads and inference, and a response may be at most 1 MiB.

owns.text: No data of its own, only the pinned model identity (name, manifest and layer digests, dimensions and bounds) as constants; vectors and their generations live in the Evie database.

interfaces.text: New(endpoint), Client.Embed(ctx, inputs), Client.Close() and ErrDisabled, plus constants such as Dimensions and BatchSize that the Evie database's dense index reads.
The endpoint comes from EVIE_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT, which the Evie database reads only when EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on.
It is used at chat time to embed one recall query alongside lexical search, and by retrieval maintenance to embed new Claim and conversation parts.

gotchas.text: Every request re-checks that EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on and returns ErrDisabled otherwise, so a strictly local feature is gated by a switch named for remote memory.
Similarity is untrusted candidate input: a dense hit only proposes, and SQLite still decides acceptance, scope, lifecycle and the text that may leave the Kernel.
At chat time the embedding call gets at most half of the 500 ms retrieval deadline (or of the caller's remaining time), far less than the client's own ten-second ceiling.
The selected manifest runs with `num_ctx=256`, so the index embeds 240-byte chunks with a 48-byte overlap after longer inputs were measured to fail with HTTP 400.
There is no remote fallback and no model download: a missing model or a changed digest fails embedding, and retrieval reports partial or unavailable coverage.

memory.spec.md calls for `Embedder` and `VectorIndex` interfaces, but in code the Evie database calls this concrete Client directly and keeps vectors in its own SQLite tables, with no interface between them.

summary.text: Implements the explicitly configured, pinned local compiler transport: a client for an Ollama server on a literal loopback address that verifies the pinned runtime and model before sending any evidence.

does.text: New takes a Config (an endpoint plus a memory.CompilerGeneration), computes the generation's identity, and accepts only `http://` with a literal loopback IP and an explicit port, with no credentials, path, query or fragment.
Its transport uses no proxy and no keep-alives, a five-second dial timeout and a 120-second response-header timeout, and refuses redirects.

VerifyCompilerConfiguration checks within five seconds, using metadata calls only, that the runtime version, the single model artifact digest, the prompt template, an empty system prompt, the quantization and the tokenizer hash all match the pinned generation.

Extract, for the memory compiler, checks the generation identity and input budget, verifies the configuration, renders the pinned template with the request and extraction schema, and calls `/api/generate` raw and non-streaming with the schema as the output format and the generation's seed, temperature, context and output limits.

Chat, for the local background memory pass, verifies the configuration and sends a system and a user message to `/api/chat` in JSON format, returning the reply with its prompt and output token counts.
It rejects any reply that is not finished with `done_reason: stop` from the pinned model, so a truncated or wrong-model answer never counts as output.

owns.text: No durable data: only the endpoint, a server identity made of the endpoint, runtime version and manifest digest, and the generation id; Memory Candidates and coverage live in the Evie database.

interfaces.text: Ollama satisfies two consumer-owned interfaces: eviedb.CompilerExtractor (ServerIdentity and Extract) and memorybackground.LocalCompleter (Chat).
It is built from the JSON file named by EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG, for the compiler host and the local background pass, or from `evie memory-compile --config` for one owner-selected range.

It returns eviedb.ErrCompilerConfiguration for an identity or pin mismatch and eviedb.ErrCompilerEndpointUnavailable for transport failures, 5xx and 429, so the Kernel can tell a misconfiguration from an unavailable endpoint.

gotchas.text: memory.spec.md describes the compiler endpoint as a loopback or Unix-socket OpenAI-compatible server such as Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp, but the code speaks Ollama's own API (`/api/generate`, `/api/chat`, `/api/show`, `/api/tags`, `/api/version`) and accepts loopback HTTP only, not Unix sockets.
There is no default model or installed configuration: without EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG nothing runs locally, and explicit memory operations keep working.
Responses are size-bounded, with separate limits for metadata and generation, and strictly framed: duplicate keys are rejected even though the runtime may add fields.
With a pinned seed and temperature a truncated reply repeats on retry, so the background pass counts ErrRuntimeOutputInvalid as malformed and eventually skips the batch.
The rendered prompt must fit the generation's proven context: rendered bytes times tokens per byte, plus template overhead and output tokens, may not exceed the context size.
Extract reports `not_dispatched` release evidence when it refuses before calling the runtime, and `completed` once the runtime has answered.

summary.text: The shared contract package for Evie's memory layers: the event, session, scope and turn-lease types of Episodic Memory, the content-free request records of Working Memory, and the typed proposals, results and queries of Semantic Memory, plus the deterministic rules every package that touches memory must apply the same way.

does.text: Defines the provider-neutral event envelope (EventInput in, Event out with session, sequence, parent and execution IDs) and its event types, from user_message and assistant_message through tool, approval and terminal events to context_snapshot, context_compacted and the in-turn context_turn_compacted; every conversation's Episodic Memory is a chain of these.

Validates what those events carry: a terminal turn payload names its stage and classification, a rolling compaction summary must fill seven fixed section headings within 16 KiB, and a context snapshot is a content-free manifest of one exact provider request.
Defines who a conversation is and what it may see: Session, Workspace and Project records and the immutable ScopeContext a session derives for itself, always owned by the single local owner.

ResolveMemoryDestination turns a recommended applicability (everywhere, workspace, session, or none) into a concrete scope key derived from the session's own Workspace or project, so a scope ID never comes from model text.

Defines the closed Semantic Memory vocabulary: six Typed Literal kinds, Predicate cardinality one or many, affirmed or denied Claim Polarity, append-only lifecycle states, source authority and evidence locators, error or changed corrections, three Graph Link relations and four lifecycle actions.

Defines each Prepare and Apply pair the Kernel offers as request, proposal and result types (remember a literal, remember an Entity relation, correct, promote, link, change a lifecycle, set standing); every proposal carries its target scope, the full scope vector with prior Scope Revisions, generated IDs and the exact proposal and prepared hashes.

Owns the standing tier's rules: a closed ClaimKind whose default is standing for every kind but fact, the <standing-memory> block rendered from Global to Workspace or project to this conversation with one JSON line per memory, repeats and secret-flagged items left out, and the 500-token budgets that refuse an approval with "memory full".

Owns the explicit-request rule for proactive memory: HasExplicitMemoryCue scans the owner's message for a closed list of English cues (remember, save, note, keep in mind, don't forget and a few more), and only a cue plus the model's requested_by_owner shows the approval card; anything else is queued for review.

Defines the review inbox and background-pass records: QueuedMemoryProposal holds exactly one prepared remember, correction or retirement plus an optional Global version, and the background types describe a due conversation, its owner-message batch, the comparison pool, a run, its commit and the owner-facing status.

Defines retrieval: RetrievalQuery (requests only, never authority), sourced RetrievalEvidence and its reference form, result statuses that tell an empty search from a failed or exhausted one, and the content-free RetrievalReceipt a context snapshot records.

FindRecallTimeReference reads one explicit past time in a request ("yesterday", "last week", "three days ago", "in March", "2026-09-14") without a model, and Window resolves it to a half-open range in the owner's time zone; retrieval only prefers evidence inside it and never widens what a reader may see.

Defines the Stage 4 compiler contracts: a pinned Compiler Generation whose identity hashes the model, tokenizer and template digests and every policy, the sealed CompilerRequest window of selected sources and recorded omissions, untrusted ExtractorCandidate output and the stored Memory Candidate.

DecodeCompilerJSON is the strict decoder both the compiler and the background pass use for model output: one object, no duplicate or unknown keys, every field present under its canonical name, at most 128 KiB.

Defines owner candidate review: a CandidateRef pins one interpretation and review revision, a ReviewPreview binds a complete atomic group by hash, and an accepted review becomes an OwnerReviewOperation, Semantic Operation schema version 6.

HasRetrievalSecret is the one secret fence (private keys, sk-, GitHub and AWS key shapes, password and token assignments) that retrieval results, the standing block, background candidates and inbox proposals all pass through.

owns.text: Holds no tables and no handles: every type here is persisted by eviedb, and the only disk access is CanonicalProjectRoot resolving a project folder through symlinks.
Owns the canonical Claim text used wherever memories are shown or compared, "subject — predicate: value" with a Denied: prefix for denied polarity, never the source's own words.
Owns the content-free receipts each context_snapshot stores: the standing block's Claim IDs, byte count and SHA-256, and the retrieval receipt's evidence references and status.

Owns the versioned constants other packages record: compaction prompt versions compaction-v2 and turn-compaction-v1, compiler policies such as owner-assertions-v1, and the token arithmetic that converts budgets with a calibrated bytes-per-token ratio.

interfaces.text: It declares no interfaces of its own: consumers own the seams and speak these types, as the Memory Plugin's SemanticMemoryKernel, the agent's SemanticMemory and MemoryRetrieval, and the background pass's Store do, and *eviedb.Store implements them all.
TurnLease, with its holder, fencing token and generation, is the write fence every Apply and every background commit takes; UnexpiredAt only reads a snapshot and never proves durable ownership.

ApprovalPayload binds an owner decision to the proposal and prepared hashes, and ProposalHashes carries the same proposal with "Always applies" switched, so the owner can flip the switch and still approve exactly what was shown.
MemoryProposalApproval, MemoryProposalResult and BackgroundStatus are the JSON contracts of the web Memory review area and `evie memory-background status`.

gotchas.text: The package is broader than its name: Workspace explore, build and merge-check settings, project root resolution and terminal-safe display labels live here because sessions and scopes do.

A Claim accepted before the standing tier has no classification and reads as a fact that is not standing; nothing is rewritten, and an approved memory_set_standing is the only way to make that Claim standing.

The standing budget counts only what the approving session sees, so another conversation's session-scoped standing memories are not counted when a Global memory is approved, and a later conversation can render slightly over 500 tokens; nothing is ever truncated.

A cue alone is not a request: "Do you remember…?" contains "remember", so the model must also set requested_by_owner; a requested_by_owner the message does not support goes to the inbox with reason no_explicit_cue.

RetrievalQuery's Relevance and RecallTime are set only by Automatic Recall, and its anchor, covered and refresh references have no JSON form, so model arguments cannot set them; the turn clears and refills the anchor and covered set itself before every search.
Hard Erasure is not implemented: the semantic projection tables are append-only by trigger, and Retirement is the only way to take knowledge out of ordinary recall, as ADR 0050 planned.

Stage evolution, compared with the original drawing: the original shows three stages and says future retrieval "may supply sourced context; Stage 3 does not inject it"; today the compiler, the background pass, the review inbox, retrieval, Automatic Recall, the standing block and session episodes all exist; the standing block reaches every request and Automatic Recall adds evidence at the start of each turn.

Turn context flow, compared with the original: each request now also carries the working-folder note, repository instructions, the standing block and a memory evidence message before the active root; compaction may be in-turn as well as rolling; a provider context-length rejection gets one compact-and-retry; and a committed compaction is offered to the background pass.

Semantic write path, compared with the original: the original has one entry, an explicit owner request shown on a card; today three reach Apply (the approval card, the review inbox for proactive and background proposals, and owner review of compiler candidates), and an inbox approval appends its approval event and runs Apply as two separate writes under the source conversation's lease.

Apply re-reads the stored approval event and compares its hashes only for new Graph Links, lifecycle changes that touch a Graph Link (schema version 5), standing changes and Promotions; remember, correct and ordinary retire or restore operations rely on their caller having stored the approval first, and check the lease, hashes, idempotency key, source event and scope vector instead.

Semantic domain model, compared with the original and the Stage 3 spec: both describe cached current-state columns as a disposable read optimization, but the projection tables are append-only by trigger, so a lifecycle or eligibility column keeps its creation value and current state comes from the latest semantic_state_events row; Claim classifications and the projection quarantine are tables the original does not show.

Graph Link endpoints and state events name their object by kind and ID, so they have no foreign keys and the data diagram draws no line from them to the Claims, Entities or Source Links they point at.

Scope and promotion, compared with the original: it says model text cannot select scope and only explicit Promotion widens reuse; today a remember may carry a destination recommendation that approval confirms, so a Workspace conversation can save straight to Global, the background pass offers a "Save everywhere instead" version, and earlier conversations of the same Context Scope are searchable as excerpts (ADR 0066).

Temporal lifecycle, compared with the original: unsupported is drawn as a lifecycle state, but it is never stored; it is computed at read time for an active Claim with no eligible Source Link. A superseded Claim cannot be restored, and a changed correction leaves the old Claim answering for valid times before the effective time while an error correction hides it.

Replay and recovery, compared with the original and ADR 0060: the shadow is a full VACUUM INTO copy of the database in a private temporary folder, replayed by calling the production Apply methods under a replay lease; startup checks quarantine scopes too; and a successful rebuild clears every quarantine row, not only the scopes it found divergent.

The original Structurizr model predates the compiler, retrieval, the background pass and the standing tier; its "Conformance Evaluation" container is today the memoryeval package and the tests that load it, and its Memory Plugin adapters live in internal/plugins.

summary.text: How one owner turn builds every provider request from durable state, redrawn from today's turn loop: lease, root user_message, history reload, standing memory and Automatic Recall, composition and compaction, a content-free snapshot, a lease-authorized provider call, and the fenced tool lifecycle, repeated until the model answers without tools.

Acquires the 30-second turn lease; a heartbeat renews it every 10 seconds
Appends the owner's text as the root user_message before any provider or tool work
Reloads accepted events (decoding only those new since the last request) and reconstructs the compaction chain
Reads repository instructions once per turn and the standing set for every request
First iteration only: Automatic Recall searches accepted memory and conversation excerpts
Composes: instructions, working-folder note, repository guidance, standing block, summary, bounded history, memory evidence before the active root, then working context
Measures the request; one automatic compaction decision per iteration, whole-turn or in-turn
When required, appends a validated context_compacted or context_turn_compacted summary
Offers the compaction's frontier to the background pass, without waiting
Revalidates held memory evidence, then appends context_snapshot: counts, frontiers, hashes and receipts, never content
Re-authorizes the lease immediately before the provider starts
Streams the composed request
Chat Completions (or Responses) over HTTPS
Streamed response; a transient failure is retried only before any output streamed
Appends assistant_message; without tool calls this is the turn's durable success
Appends a tool_intent for each call
Prepare, approve, execute, with the lease re-authorized before preparation and before execution
Appends the approval (with proposal and prepared hashes for memory) and the terminal tool outcome
Recomposes from the newly accepted events and loops
On a durable failure appends turn_failed or turn_interrupted; always releases the lease
