Never read: other sessions' memory, sibling Workspaces and projects, quarantined scopes
Conversation excerpts: earlier conversations of the same Context Scope only
Destination recommendation: everywhere, workspace or session, resolved from the session and shown on approval
Background Global version: Save everywhere instead
Narrower accepted Claim (session, Workspace or project) stays unchanged
Promotion proposal: active Claim with eligible sources, source and destination revisions
Broader Claim with reused or created Entities and copied Source Links
semantic_promotions and promotion entities map source to destination

edges.label: background ADD Evie thinks holds everywhere
ID-level provenance; unreadable source text withheld

summary.text: The lifecycle of one Claim, redrawn from today's code: states are appended as semantic_state_events under Transaction Time and never edited, while Valid Time says when the Claim holds in the world; exact reads ask valid_at, as_known_at or both, and only an active Claim with an eligible Source Link is current.

states.label: active and supported: in current reads within its Valid Time
unsupported (computed): active, but no eligible Source Link
retired: hidden from current reads, kept for history
superseded by a changed correction: still answers for valid times before the effective time
superseded by an error correction: never current again

transitions.label: retire_memory (an Entity's retirement lists its dependents)
restore_memory, only if its dependencies are still legal
retract_source of its last eligible Source Link
restore_source while the Claim is active
retire_memory (the latest state is still active)
correct_claim, mode changed: old Valid Time ends where the replacement's begins
correct_claim, mode error: the replacement inherits the old Valid Time

summary.text: How the live semantic projection is checked and repaired, redrawn from today's code: accepted operations are the canonical history, a cheap check runs on every database open, the owner's /memory verify replays them into a private copy and compares per scope, divergent scopes are quarantined, and /memory rebuild swaps in a verified projection under a fenced lock.

nodes.label: semantic_operations: accepted history, schema versions 1 to 7
Live projection rows
Every open: revision and state-event frontiers, known schema versions, semantic foreign keys
VACUUM INTO a private temporary database
Shadow replay: reset the projection, re-run each operation's Apply in scope-frontier order
Unknown kind or version, or a gap in a scope frontier: replay fails at that operation
Compare per scope: canonical row hashes, revisions, operation frontiers, foreign keys
Match: live state stays in service
Quarantine affected scopes: their reads and writes fail; other scopes and Episodic Memory keep working
/memory rebuild: fenced maintenance lock, self-verified shadow, foreign-key check
One transaction: replace projection rows, restore append-only triggers, clear quarantine

summary.text: Runs the background memory pass, off unless EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on with OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG for a local extractor: when a root conversation goes idle, gathers 20 new owner messages, or has owner messages a committed compaction summarized, it reads only those owner messages, extracts candidate memories, compares them with existing ones, and queues exact ADD, UPDATE or INVALIDATE proposals in the owner's review inbox without applying anything.

does.text: FromEnv resolves the configuration and never fails: OpenRouter when EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on and OPENROUTER_API_KEY are set, otherwise the pinned local extractor named by EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG, otherwise disabled, and any bad setting disables the pass with a reason the owner can act on.

Run ticks every minute until shutdown; each Tick records the activation frontier once, takes the cross-process runner lease, stops when today's spend has reached a cap, and runs at most four due conversations one at a time, renewing the runner lease before each.

RequestCompactionFlush only wakes a sleeping Run early; a committed compaction makes its conversation due by itself, and a compaction-due conversation runs pass after pass up to the compaction's frontier (at most 64).

Each pass reads a bounded batch of the conversation's owner messages since its cursor (30 messages, 24 KiB, each cut at 4 KiB with a visible marker); a message with a detected secret or a local slash command moves the cursor but is never sent.

Extract: one JSON-mode call asks for at most eight owner-subject memories, each with kind, applicability, Predicate token and label, cardinality, one typed value, polarity and the index of the stating message, listing the Predicate tokens already in use so they are reused.

Route: in a Global conversation every memory targets Global and a Workspace memory is dropped; in a Workspace or project conversation every memory stays in that scope, and "profile" only marks Evie's suggestion that it holds everywhere.

Compare: the conversation's readable current memories and pending remembers are ranked by a deterministic lexical score (same Predicate token, label, value and text overlap) plus a small boost when the full-text or dense retriever also returns the Claim, keeping the top eight above a 0.25 floor.

Decide: an exact duplicate is a NOOP and a candidate with nothing similar is an ADD without a model call; the rest go to one decision call that chooses ADD, UPDATE (changed or error), INVALIDATE or NOOP against memories shown under short handles.

Prepare: ADD goes through PrepareRememberLiteral, UPDATE through PrepareCorrectClaim (a changed correction takes the stating message's time as its effective time) and INVALIDATE through a retire PrepareMemoryLifecycle, the same Kernel paths an approval card uses.
For a Workspace or project ADD that Evie thinks holds everywhere, it also prepares the Global version under the same idempotency key, so approving either version resolves the proposal.

Commit: it takes the conversation's turn lease for ten seconds, retrying up to twelve times five seconds apart, and queues the proposals and moves the cursor in one compare-and-set transaction; a conversation busy for the whole minute defers the run.

Status reports the configuration, today's spend and what remains, the last run and last problem, skipped batches, pending background proposals, each recent conversation's cursor and the compaction flushes still owed, without any message, proposal or memory text.

owns.text: Holds no tables: its durable state is eviedb's activation and runner-lease row, one cursor per root conversation and one row per run, and its proposals land in the review inbox.
Owns the extraction and decision prompts and their strict output contracts, versioned memory-background-v1 and recorded with the model identity on every run.

Owns spend accounting: before each call it reserves the estimated input (three bytes per token) plus the whole output allowance against a 32,000-token pass budget and today's caps of 300,000 tokens and $0.25, priced from the OpenRouter catalog or a deliberately high fallback.

Owns the idempotency keys of its proposals, derived from the conversation, the stating message and the proposed change, so a pass repeated after a crash proposes the identical change under the identical key.
In memory a Runner keeps only its holder ID, the current price, whether it has activated, and a one-slot channel that wakes it for a flush.

interfaces.text: Store is the consumer-owned persistence seam (activation, runner lease, due conversations, batch, pool, the three Prepare calls, turn lease, commit, failure, spend and progress); *eviedb.Store implements it.
Searcher is optional: when the store also offers SearchMemory, its accepted-memory hits boost similarity, and when it fails only the boost is lost.

Model is one structured completion (Identity and Complete) that must not retry; OpenRouterModel sends Chat Completions with JSON output, temperature 0, low reasoning and no tools, and LocalModel uses the loopback extractor's chat.
Runner satisfies the agent's CompactionMemoryFlush, and cmd/evie hands it to every REPL and serve conversation so committed compactions are offered to the pass.

gotchas.text: It reads only owner user messages of root conversations, never assistant, tool, web, compiler or delegated text, so third-party text cannot plant a fact about the owner; a delegated conversation never offers a compaction flush.

It never commits while a live turn holds the conversation: the turn lease fences the commit, and the cursor's compare-and-set makes a pass that another process already covered record itself as superseded, only so its spend still counts.

A pending proposal is never changed, a Claim outside the conversation's own Context Scope cannot be corrected or retired from it, a Claim gets at most one change per pass, and an identical retired or superseded Claim is skipped because restoring it is the owner's explicit act.
Only literal memories are extracted; an Entity-to-Entity memory still needs the in-turn memory_remember_entity tool.

Three consecutive malformed replies, or a batch that cannot fit the pass budget, skip the batch: the cursor moves past it and the skipped run stays visible; a provider or network failure never skips, and backs the conversation off from one minute doubling to one hour.

Only a failure that proved nothing was generated (no response, 429, 502, 503 or 504) is retried, twice, honoring Retry-After but never waiting more than 30 seconds; shutdown cancels the in-flight call and commits nothing, and the cursor lets the next process redo the batch.

The memory architecture plan suggested the model's cheaper :batch variant, but ValidateRemoteModel refuses it, as it does floating latest aliases and the auto router, because the pass does not use OpenRouter's asynchronous Batch API.

The plan's decision 4 routes each proposal to profile or Workspace scope; since the 2026-10-12 amendment the code keeps a Workspace or project conversation's memories in that scope and offers Global only as a second version.
The package comment names only the idle and turn triggers; the compaction flush is a third trigger that ignores both.
The spec says background proposals are labelled "Found in your conversations" in the review inbox; the web inbox has no such label and only marks a proposal whose owner message held no explicit cue.
Real-model proposal precision and recall are unmeasured: the package's precision probe scripts the model's mistakes and so measures only the deterministic filtering layers.

summary.text: The path of one pass over one conversation and the five run outcomes it can record; only a succeeded or skipped run moves the conversation's cursor.

states.label: due: compaction owed, 20 owner messages, or idle 10 minutes
waiting for the conversation's turn lease
deferred: cursor kept, batch read again later
skipped: cursor moved past a persistently malformed batch
superseded: another pass covered the batch; spend recorded

transitions.label: runner lease held and under today's caps
only withheld messages or commands: nothing to send
provider or store failure, or malformed output below the skip threshold
third consecutive malformed reply or over the pass budget
daily cap reached between calls, or shutdown after spending
a live turn kept the conversation for twelve attempts
cursor moved: another pass committed first

summary.text: Holds the versioned, model-free contracts of Evie's memory evaluations: the Stage 3 semantic conformance fixture and report, the seeded scale corpus and its scorer, and the offline Stage 4 release assessment; it runs no model, network call or capability itself.

does.text: Keeps four evaluation panels separate and in a fixed order (semantic conformance, learned extraction, retrieval provenance, answer abstention) and refuses a manifest that drops, reorders or combines them, so one score cannot hide a safety failure.

LoadManifest decodes a fixture manifest strictly, requires all 25 Stage 3 coverage items (scopes, corrections, lifecycle, Promotion, replay, restart, recovery and more), an isolated new database and typed evidence per case, and checks the manifest's own SHA-256.

Defines the conformance report: run, fixture and environment identities, per-panel and per-case results under a failure taxonomy (scope leakage, replay divergence, temporal boundary error and others), and latency metrics summarized and compared with a baseline run.

GenerateScaleCorpus builds a seeded synthetic ten-month history (corpus memory-scale-replay-v6) of personal topics, project areas, planted facts, Claims, corrections and retirements, with gold labels and probes for Automatic Recall, memory_search and conversation search.
ScoreScale grades the evidence each probe delivered as required, tolerated or unwanted into a versioned report (version 6), and ScaleTargetsFor lists which targets are met.

AssessStage4Release grades a frozen Stage 4 release submission (plan, approvals, custody, execution and numeric gates) offline from metadata and hashes; VerifyStage4Evidence binds the referenced artifacts to that exact submission.

owns.text: Holds no tables and no runtime state; its inputs are fixture files and in-memory values, and its recorded scale baselines are JSON files under its testdata.
Owns the version constants that keep comparisons honest: a baseline is only compared against the same corpus and report version.

interfaces.text: Its exported functions are used only by tests and one script: eviedb's Stage 3 conformance test loads the checked-in manifest, the package's own scale replay drives real agent turns, the Memory Plugin and SQLite with a scripted provider, and scripts/memory-stage4-release validates release metadata.
ScaleGapDenseScan mirrors the production signal memory.RetrievalGapDenseScan, and the replay test fails if the two drift apart.

gotchas.text: No production package imports it, so its contracts only run under go test and the release script, never in serve or the REPL.
A panel with no cases reports not_populated rather than passed, so a report cannot present an unexercised system as healthy.
The default scale tier is skipped under go test -short, and the large dense tier runs only with EVIE_MEMORY_SCALE_EVAL=large.
Every Stage 4 release report states its own limits: the assessment makes no model call and reads no holdout source, and retrieval and answer quality are deferred to Stage 5.

summary.text: Runs one conversation Session's turn loop: it streams a model response, stores it durably, runs the requested tools through the session's pinned Toolset, and repeats until the model answers without tools.

does.text: Send runs one turn: it refuses a second concurrent turn on the same Session with ErrBusy, acquires the session's durable turn lease, and stores the owner's text as the turn's root user_message event before any model work.

Each iteration reloads the durable history, composes the request (system prompt, working-folder note, repository instructions, standing and recalled memory, the conversation, and the tool schemas), and stores the request's shape as a context_snapshot event before calling the provider.

Streams the provider response through the Events callbacks and retries a transient failure (no response, or HTTP 429, 502, 503 or 504) at most twice, only while nothing has streamed yet, with backoff capped at 30 seconds.

Stores each assistant message as an assistant_message event; a message without tool calls is the turn's durable success, otherwise every call is stored as a tool_intent, dispatched through the Toolset, and closed with a tool_succeeded, tool_failed or tool_cancelled event before the next model request.

Bounds a turn at EVIE_TURN_STEP_LIMIT model responses (100 by default): the last permitted request goes out with tool_choice none and a harness notice asking for an answer, and a response that still asks for tools fails the turn with ErrStepLimitExceeded.
Compacts older context automatically when the composed request would exceed its working budget, and gives a provider context-length rejection exactly one compact-and-retry per turn.

Runs automatic memory recall once, on the turn's first iteration, unless the session turned it off, and reads standing memory for every request so an approval earlier in the turn applies to the next request.

Puts the harness-owned InvocationContext and the Task mutation attribution on the context of every tool call, so a tool gets the scope, lease, source event and working Directory without the model choosing them.

When a turn fails for a reason with durable meaning (provider error or invalid response, caller cancellation or deadline, context overflow, repository-instruction failure, step limit) it stores a turn_failed or turn_interrupted event naming the stage, and tells the frontend when streamed text was discarded.
Builds delegated worker sessions with NewDelegatedWithToolset: the worker's pinned instructions replace the primary system prompt, and automatic recall and model-directed memory reads are off.

owns.text: Owns the order and shape of a turn's durable events: user_message, context_snapshot, assistant_message, tool_intent, approval, the tool outcome and a terminal turn event, linked by parent event IDs.
Holds no tables of its own: every event goes through the History interface, which eviedb's SessionHistory implements against the events table, fenced by the turn lease.

Keeps per-session state in memory: the pinned Toolset, the context profile and reasoning setting, the session's working Directory, and opaque Responses continuation items that live only for the current turn.
Bounds every tool result at 100 KiB when it is stored, keeping its head and tail plus the original size and SHA-256 when it must cut.

interfaces.text: Session.Send(ctx, input, Events, tools.Approver) is the one entry point frontends call; the web server and the REPL both drive it.

Events is the frontend's rendering contract (Delta, Reasoning, ReasoningDone, AssistantDone, ToolCall, ToolResult, ResponseDiscarded); a frontend that also implements ActivityEvents gets the committed event in place of AssistantDone.
Client is the consumer-owned provider seam, one ChatStream call with streaming handlers, satisfied by the OpenRouter client.

History (Append, Events) and TurnOwnership (Acquire, Heartbeat, Authorize, Release) are consumer-owned persistence seams; the adapters bind the session and lease holder, so no method takes them as arguments.
Constructors take one resolved, immutable tools.Toolset (NewWithToolset, NewWithCompactorAndToolset, NewDelegatedWithToolset); SessionOption values may narrow reads but never widen the grant.

WrapUpSignal and CompactionMemoryFlush are optional hooks: the subagent supervisor ends a worker's turn early through the first, and the background memory pass is offered every committed compaction through the second.

gotchas.text: The turn lease lasts 30 seconds and is renewed every 10; a lost lease cancels the turn with ErrLeaseLost, and every append is fenced by the lease token, so a turn that lost its lease cannot write.
A tool call cut off by cancellation or a lost lease leaves a tool_intent with no outcome; history reconstruction drops such incomplete tool-call groups instead of replaying them.
A session given a nil Approver declines every gated tool call, which is how delegated workers run.

The agent-extract spec gave Send per-call extra tools; today's code pins one Toolset per session and rejects different extras with "session Toolset is already pinned", keeping New plus Send(extra...) only as a legacy path.
The primary system prompt is derived from the session's pinned tool schemas, so a session pinned before a tool existed keeps its exact prompt; worker instructions replace it entirely.
A committed final assistant message wins over a cancellation that arrived while its append was in flight: the turn still ends as a success.
Provider retries happen only before any output streamed; once text reached the frontend a provider failure ends the turn, and the frontend is told the streamed text was not saved.

summary.text: The stages one Send passes through, as the turn coordinator records them; a terminal turn event names the stage a failed or interrupted turn ended in.

states.label: turn_start: lease held, owner message being stored
context_compose: load history, compose the request
tool_prepare: store the intent, prepare the call
succeeded: a final assistant message is committed
failed or interrupted: turn_failed or turn_interrupted event

transitions.label: compaction failed but the projection still fits
preparation failed or unknown tool: an error result
declined or expired; approval event stored
next call of the same response
all calls answered: next model request
provider error, invalid response or step limit

summary.text: Defines every model-facing tool, one file per tool, and the immutable Toolset that dispatches a tool call through approval, lifecycle authorization and execution.

does.text: A Tool binds a wire schema to an Execute function that takes the model's raw JSON arguments and returns plain text; tools never build wire messages, the dispatcher does.
NewToolset copies every definition and schema, so a live session's capability surface cannot change underneath it; WithTools and WithoutTools return new Toolsets.
The dispatcher finds the tool by name, decides whether it needs approval, prepares the effect and its preview, asks the Approver, hands the decision to the observer, and only then executes.
It asks the caller to authorize the turn's lease at two boundaries: before preparation work that may reach a server, and before execution.
Declines, expiries, tool errors and unknown tools become ordinary model-visible tool results, with error text cut at 16 KiB.

KernelToolset is the non-plugin surface (get_time, query_db, edit_db, read_file, edit_file, bash and the cron tools) that production composition extends with plugin capabilities; of these only edit_db and edit_file need approval.

Supplies the confined worker toolsets: ExploreToolset (root-confined read_file, the read-only query_db, and a bash that runs only vetted read-only commands) and BuildToolset (worktree-confined read_file, edit_file and write_file, plus a bash only where an OS sandbox exists).
Runs the owner's setup and verify commands for the merge gate under the same OS sandbox as worker bash, and refuses to run them at all without one.
Frames third-party text (web pages, YouTube transcripts, transcript queries, stored tool results) as untrusted data before returning it.

owns.text: Keeps the bash tool's working directory in the session's Directory, falling back to a process-wide remembered directory only when no Directory is supplied.
Spills output past the inline limit (30,000 characters for bash) to unique temporary files, which are swept after 24 hours.
Holds the secrets denylist the file tools enforce for reads and writes (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gnupg, ~/.evie/procedural, shell rc files, .netrc and Evie's database files).

interfaces.text: Tool, Toolset, Approver, Decision (Declined, Approved, Expired, ApprovedAlternative), ApprovalObserver and LifecycleAuthorizer form the dispatch contract the agent loop drives.

PreparedTool carries a FileChangePreview for the approval card, ApprovalMetadata binding a semantic proposal to its durable approval, an optional Alternative, and an optional Review that queues the effect for the owner instead of asking.
InvocationContext, read with InvocationFromContext, is the harness-owned authority a tool sees: profile, Directory, scope, lease, source and intent events, memory search and stored-result reads.
Toolset.WithWorkerRoot and Toolset.WithBuildFence bind a worker's pinned folder or worktree without changing schemas, so the Toolset still matches its receipt.
ReadDB gives Workspace tabs the same fenced, read-only SELECT path as query_db.

gotchas.text: bash is deliberately ungated, with no approval and no path denylist, because a shell walks around any fence; the file tools' secrets denylist does not apply to it.
The web server's cross-origin guard exists because bash is ungated: a forged browser request must be rejected before it can start a turn.
A RequiresApproval check that errors counts as needing approval.
A prepared tool with semantic ApprovalMetadata fails unless an approval observer is wired, so a semantic change never runs without a durable approval record.
ApprovedAlternative runs the prepared alternative as an ordinary approval; for a tool without one it counts as declined.
LegacyKernelToolset and PreTodoExtractionKernelToolset exist only to rebuild old Composition Receipts; new sessions must use KernelToolset.
A build worker has no bash on a host without a usable OS sandbox, and EVIE_WORKER_SANDBOX=off turns worker bash off everywhere.
bash's process-wide fallback directory reverses the earlier decision that the tools package is stateless.

summary.text: How one model tool call moves through the dispatcher, and which durable event closes it.

states.label: preparing: approval needed, Prepare builds the effect

transitions.label: NeedsApproval, or RequiresApproval says yes or errors
Review set: queued for the owner, no approval recorded
Approver called with name, arguments and preview
approved, declined or expired; observer stores it

summary.text: The Kernel's Plugin Manager for compiled First-party Plugins: it validates their manifests, runs the reversible Plugin Lifecycle, and resolves an Agent Preset into a session's Toolset and Composition Receipt.

does.text: NewManager validates the compiled catalog once: unique plugin IDs and Capability IDs, valid manifests, a provider role for every declared capability, compatibility evidence, dependency ranges, and a dependency order without cycles.
ConfigureEnabledState seeds each plugin's default enabled state once in Evie's database and replays the owner's durable choices; every later management call refreshes from that store first.
SetEnabledWithTransition stores the owner's intent, reconciles every affected plugin, and reports the target's transition plus each dependent whose lifecycle changed.
Reconciliation stops plugins in reverse dependency order and starts them in dependency order, hiding a plugin's capabilities before any Stop hook runs.
A failed start is rolled back by calling Stop under a bounded cleanup context detached from cancellation; a failed Stop leaves the plugin failed with cleanup pending until a newer command retries it.

ResolvePresetContext composes one of the four built-in presets (standard, research, explore, build): each required Capability must come from a ready provider within its contract range, an unavailable optional one only warns, and duplicate tool names fail.
Builds the session's Composition Receipt from the selected providers, capabilities, schema hashes, tool schemas, instruction hashes and configuration references, and validates it before returning.

ResumeCompositionContext rebuilds a pinned session exactly from its receipt, choosing the historical preset content by its version hash, and accepts a newer provider only with exact contract and schema evidence, returning a Compatibility Resolution for it.
Ships ten first-party plugins (web, finance, youtube, todo, memory, subagents, workflows, github, mcp and workspace-tabs), each enabled by default until the owner chooses otherwise.

owns.text: Owns the in-memory lifecycle record of each compiled plugin: enabled and started flags, state, diagnostic, warnings, active capabilities, loaded optional dependencies and Connection Readiness.
Stores only desired enabled state, through the EnabledStateStore boundary, which eviedb implements as plugin_enabled_configuration rows whose revision grows with every command.
Owns the built-in Agent Presets and every historical standard preset version, each identified by the SHA-256 of its canonical content.

interfaces.text: Plugin (Manifest, Start, Stop) is the one small lifecycle interface; contributions go through focused provider roles: ToolProvider, ResumableToolProvider, WorkflowCapabilityProvider, WorkflowEffectProvider and ConnectionReadinessProvider.
Manifest declares the plugin ID, implementation version, Kernel compatibility range, required and optional dependencies, Capability Contracts, and the prior implementations it can resume.
Management reads: InspectContext lists every plugin's lifecycle, health, Connection Readiness and diagnostics, and InspectPresetsContext and ValidatePresetContext report Preset Validity.
Plugins reach Kernel services through narrow interfaces of their own, such as the Subagents plugin's ResearchSupervisor.
CanonicalTodoMutationAttempt exposes the Todo wire contract's idempotency and request identities for evaluation.

gotchas.text: Production sessions are composed through Agent Presets; NewSessionToolset, which would add every ready capability, is not used by the commands.
ADR 0012 and the plugins spec describe user-authored presets versioned in procedural Git; the code has only the four immutable built-ins and refuses any other preset ID.
ADR 0036 and the plugins spec give presets a lazily loaded skill catalog; Preset has no skill field and nothing loads skills.
The plugins spec says Phase 1 implements only the tool-provider role; the Manager already accepts workflow read and effect providers.
A Capability's provider is the part of its ID before the first dot, so every Capability ID must be namespaced by its plugin.
Connection Readiness never affects lifecycle or Preset Validity: a plugin that needs account setup still loads and its preset still resolves.
Ready is not visible: a ready plugin's capabilities reach a session only when its Agent Preset names them.
The command revision makes a same-value enable meaningful: it retries a failed start or pending cleanup instead of being ignored.
A session whose receipt pins a capability of a plugin that is no longer ready cannot be reopened: resume requires every pinned provider to be ready and fails visibly otherwise.

Disabling a plugin leaves already-open sessions' Toolsets intact, because a Toolset copies its tool definitions; whether those tools still work is up to the provider's Stop, as when the Subagents supervisor refuses new work once stopped.
Reconciliation gives up after four passes per plugin plus one and reports that the lifecycle did not stabilize.

summary.text: The seven externally observable states the Plugin Manager moves a compiled plugin through.

states.label: waiting: enabled, required dependency not ready
failed: start failed, or cleanup pending

transitions.label: disabled, stopped, a required dependency leaving, or optional availability changed
a newer command retries pending cleanup
re-enabled after a clean failed start
still enabled and not manually stopped: restarted
disabled after a clean failed start

summary.text: Defines the Composition Receipt, the content-free durable identity of what one session was composed from, and the Compatibility Resolution that records a provider substitution.

does.text: Validate checks a receipt completely: format version 1, a canonical preset identity with a sha256: version, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH versions, no repeated providers, capabilities or tool schemas, and every Capability naming a listed provider it is namespaced by.
Marshal validates before encoding, and Unmarshal rejects unknown fields and trailing JSON before validating.
ValidateCompatibilityResolution accepts a substitution only by a strictly newer implementation of the same provider, with a timestamp and per-Capability contract and schema evidence.
Provides the identity rules shared by providers and persistence: ValidIdentity, ValidProviderID, ValidCapabilityID, and strict semantic-version parsing and comparison.

owns.text: Owns the receipt schema: preset ID and version, Evie version, providers with implementation versions, capabilities with contract versions and schema hashes, tool schema hashes, instruction hashes, configuration references and warnings.

Owns the closed vocabulary of warnings for an optional Capability left out: provider not compiled, disabled, stopped, waiting or failed, capability not exposed, contract incompatible, or provider contract invalid.
Stores nothing itself: eviedb keeps one receipt per session in session_composition_receipts and appends Compatibility Resolutions separately.

interfaces.text: Receipt, Provider, Capability, ToolSchema, InstructionReference, ConfigurationReference and Warning are plain JSON structs, which plugins re-exports as its own receipt type names.
Clone copies a receipt's slices so callers cannot alias a pinned receipt.
CompatibilityResolutionKey, MarshalCompatibilityResolution and UnmarshalCompatibilityResolution give resolutions a stable identity and strict encoding.

gotchas.text: The only configuration reference kind is connection, and its ID must be a canonical UUID, so a receipt cannot carry a credential or a free-form setting.
It imports neither providers nor persistence, so both can consume one closed schema without a cycle.
Instructions are pinned by ID and SHA-256 only; a receipt never holds instruction text.
A saved receipt never changes: a substitution is recorded as a separate Compatibility Resolution rather than by rewriting the receipt.

summary.text: Supervises bounded child agents inside the Kernel: delegated research, explore and build workers for a parent turn, and run-owned workers for a Workflow Run.

does.text: Delegate, Explore and Build validate a batch against the Policy, derive the worker's receipt from the parent's own pinned receipt, admit every child durably, then run them in parallel and wait for all of them.
A child starts only when per-parent and runtime-wide capacity allow, checked in a write transaction, and fails with queue_deadline if it waits longer than the policy deadline.

Each child is an ordinary agent Session over its own child session, built with NewDelegatedWithToolset and a metered model client that authorizes every call, enforces the token and request-size budgets, and asks for a tool-free wrap-up at 90 percent of a budget.
A watchdog re-checks the child's authority every 100 ms and cancels it once a durable check proves that authority gone.
Settles every attempt with a terminal state and reason; an outcome the store cannot record is retried, then handed to recovery and to same-key retries.
Continue resumes a finished child's own session as a new attempt with a fresh budget, under the current parent turn's authority.

For a build worker it prepares the git worktree, runs the owner's setup command with network on the base commit, fences the tools to the worktree, and commits the worker's changes on its branch whatever the outcome.
Runs the merge gate: ProposeMerge verifies the branch offline, rebases it onto the target and verifies again, and Merge fast-forwards the target only for the exact proposal the owner approved.
RunRecovery reconciles abandoned attempts and interrupted gate steps for the whole process lifetime, and never starts a child or a model call.
RunWorker runs a worker for a Workflow Run's agent step under the run's fenced lease and the step's pinned Model Policy, refusing when the worker preset no longer composes to what the run pinned.

owns.text: Owns only in-process supervision state: active calls, outcomes awaiting a write, build commit reports, gates running in this process, and target-branch moves to tell running workers about.
Durable attempt records live in Evie's database through eviedb's subagent_executions, admitted, started and settled in immediate transactions.
Each child's conversation is an ordinary session with its own events, created at admission with the delegating session as its parent.

interfaces.text: New(store, policy) and Configure(client, profile, resolver) set the supervisor up; the Subagents plugin's Start and Stop enable it and drain it.
Resolver composes a worker preset fresh, or exactly from a pinned receipt, into its Toolset, receipt and pinned instructions.
The Supervisor satisfies plugins.ResearchSupervisor (Delegate, Explore, Build, ReadReport, Continue, ProposeMerge, Merge) without the plugins package importing it.
MergeAsOwner and CloseAsOwner let the owner merge or close a build's Change from the Changes tab or the command line.

gotchas.text: Children run with no Approver, so any approval-gated tool a child calls is declined.

A child never gets more than its parent: research and build receipts copy the parent's pinned capability versions, and explore and build require the parent to hold the tools theirs are narrower forms of.
The package doc speaks of foreground children, but run-owned workers run for a Workflow Run, under its lease and node attempt, with no parent turn at all.
Delivery rechecks data access after the last child settles; a child that cannot be delivered becomes an error entry without its content, while its siblings are still returned.
A pinned build worker that had bash will not resume on a host without an OS sandbox, rather than get an unsandboxed shell.
SQLite lock contention (SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_LOCKED) proves nothing about authority, so the supervisor retries it instead of ending a child.

summary.text: The durable states of one delegated or run-owned worker attempt, as subagent_executions records them.

states.label: partial: wrap-up report after a budget ran low

transitions.label: capacity free and the owner's authority holds
queue_deadline: waited past the policy deadline
parent cancelled or supervisor shut down
child turn ended with an answer
time, token, context or step budget triggered the wrap-up
deadline, token budget, context limit, wrap-up failed or infrastructure
recovery: the owning lease is no longer live

summary.text: Defines the durable records and contracts of delegated work, kept separate from Tasks: assignments, policies, attempts, results as the parent reads them, build reports and the merge gate.

does.text: Names the delegation tools and their subagents.* Capability IDs: delegate_research, read_subagent_report, continue_research, delegate_explore, delegate_build and propose_build_merge.

Policy bounds delegation by per-parent and runtime-wide concurrency, batch size, children per turn, a deadline, a token budget and byte limits; DefaultPolicy is 2 per parent, 4 at once, 8 per batch, 16 per turn, 15 minutes and one million tokens.
Policy.Validate and ValidateWorkerBatch refuse a bad policy or batch before any child or provider is touched, naming the setting, key, field and limit.
Result.ParentView renders a result for the parent model: harness-written fields stay plain JSON, and everything the child wrote becomes one untrusted-data frame labelled with the execution ID.
MergeProposal.ParentView frames verification output as untrusted data, and ApprovalCard renders the merge approval card the owner sees.
ChangeText.Check bounds a Change's title to one printable line of 72 characters and its description to 4,096 bytes.

owns.text: Owns the Attempt record: dispatch and execution IDs, parent authority, assignment and digest, child session, pinned receipt and policy, state and times, wrap-up, continuation, explore root, build worktree, gate, run owner and result.
Owns the attempt states (admitted, running, succeeded, partial, failed, cancelled, interrupted) and the reasons a child stopped; eviedb enforces the same list in a CHECK constraint.
Owns the merge-gate record: the step, the setup and verify runs with their outcomes, target and branch heads, and the merge.
Owns RunOwner, a run-owned worker's authority: the Workflow Run's lease holder and token, the node attempt, and the step's pinned Model Policy.

interfaces.text: Parent is the live invocation the harness supplies (profile, scope, lease, source and intent events); the model cannot set it.
AdmitsChildren and BindsParentLease say which committed tool intents may authorize children or record the parent's lease.

Error sentinels (ErrConflict, ErrCapacity, ErrAuthority, ErrPolicy, ErrNotFound, ErrNotResumable, ErrUnavailable, ErrWorkerChanged) are the shared failure contract of the store, the supervisor and the plugin.
RunAssignment, RunOutcome and RunKey are the Workflow Runtime's contract for run-owned workers.

gotchas.text: ErrNotFound deliberately does not distinguish a missing execution from another session's, so an execution ID reveals nothing.
A batch of max_batch results at result_bytes each must fit a 96 KiB envelope, under the agent loop's 100 KiB tool-result bound, and Validate rejects a policy that would not.
Fields added later (Path, Base, Worker and others) are omitted when empty, so earlier records and assignment digests stay byte-identical.
A build child's commands are worker-written, so ParentBuild leaves them out of the plain JSON and they appear only inside the framed summary.
Attempts stay separate from Tasks: a Task names no execution, and orchestration joins them only when it reads a Task's latest build.

summary.text: The steps a build attempt's merge gate records; recovery settles an in-progress step whose owner's turn is gone.

states.label: verifying: the branch as the worker left it
merge_refused: the owner's checkout would be overwritten

setup skipped: base commit not in the owner's history
verify failed, timed out, or changed tracked files
branch rebased onto a newer head
branch already contained the head: second run skipped

summary.text: Defines the Kernel-owned contract for durable Tasks and Task Trees: their fields, validation, status rules, idempotent mutation identities, and the pure read model orchestration uses to dispatch work.

does.text: Validates every mutation input before persistence: non-blank titles, priorities 0 to 5, YYYY-MM-DD due dates, positive revisions, idempotency keys of at most 256 bytes, and at most 100 children per decomposition.
ValidateStatusTransition allows any change among open, in_progress and blocked and into completed or cancelled, while a completed or cancelled Task can only be reopened.
Every update is a compare-and-swap on the Task's revision, and a stale revision is a ConflictError.

Computes canonical SHA-256 request identities for create, decompose, update, claim and release, so a retried mutation under the same idempotency key is recognized and a different request under that key is refused.
Plans Task Trees with dependencies between Tasks of one tree and expected paths, rejecting dependency cycles, including waiting on an ancestor or a descendant.

Plan.Readiness computes todo_ready's read model: dispatchable Tasks in batches whose paths do not conflict, sized by DispatchLimits.Capacity, plus in-flight builds, blocked Tasks with reasons, and active Tasks whose work looks finished.

owns.text: Owns the Task shape: ID, parent and root, sibling order, scope, title, description, priority, due date, result summary, dependencies, paths, status and revision.
Owns the audit vocabulary of Task events: operation, actor, session, run, revisions, outcome, diagnostic code, claim and grant IDs, and management override.
Owns the delegated-access record: an AccessGrant at read, contribute or manage level for one child-session execution, ended rather than deleted.
Persists nothing itself: eviedb implements Service and chooses identities and authority-bearing fields.

interfaces.text: Service is the focused persistence boundary first-party plugins consume: create, list, get, tree, update, decompose, claim, release and claim lookup.

MutationAttribution carries actor, session, run, parent session, Workspace or project and the lease fence; the agent loop installs it with WithMutationAttribution just before a tool runs, and it is never a model argument.
Typed errors such as InputError, NotFoundError, ConflictError, TransitionError and ClaimHeldError unwrap to package sentinels so callers can classify failures.
ReadyQuery's dispatch limits and turn source are trusted inputs from the runtime, never model arguments.

gotchas.text: Task Focus is a trusted projection anchor (ListFilter.FocusID) that model-facing schemas never expose, and it grants no access.
A Task Claim needs full lease attribution (holder, token and generation) from a still-active execution, and eviedb refuses claim-requiring updates without one.
Delegated sessions can neither create Task Tree roots nor use management overrides.
Paths only keep conflicting work apart; they never grant or fence file access, and omitting them means a Task may touch any file.
Readiness schedules nothing: the orchestrating model dispatches inside its own turn, and the harness re-checks the same rules when it admits a build worker.
A dependency counts as done only when its Task is completed and its build is merged or has nothing to merge, so dependent work starts from the merged result.

summary.text: The statuses a Task moves between; ValidateStatusTransition allows any change among active statuses and only reopening from a finished one.
Derives a stable, content-free evidence baseline for evaluating durable Tasks; it does not score model quality or store reports.

does.text: Derive counts Tasks, completions (completed), abandonments (cancelled), accepted decompositions, rejected revision conflicts, and claim releases made by recovery or because the execution ended.
Joins each Task event to the episodic tool evidence of the same session and execution: the tool intent, the approval if any, and the outcome.
Groups Todo tool intents by canonical idempotency identity to count retries of the same request, duplicate attempts, and different requests reusing one key.
Sorts evidence links by session, execution and Task event, so the same input always yields the same report.

owns.text: Owns the Report schema, version 1: counts plus EvidenceLink entries.
EvidenceLink holds correlation identities only and deliberately excludes prompts, reasoning, tool arguments and results, Task content and credentials.
Stores nothing: the caller supplies the Input and receives the Report.

interfaces.text: Derive(Input) (Report, error) is the whole interface; Input carries Tasks, Task events, episodic events and each session's Task scope.

gotchas.text: No production code imports it; its only caller is its own test, so the baseline is computed only under go test.
It reuses the Todo plugin's strict argument decoders to canonicalize attempts, so a change to the Todo wire contract changes what counts as a retry.
Todo arguments that fail to decode are skipped rather than reported, and only a todo_add without a resolvable context scope is an error.
ConflictCount adds rejected revision conflicts and different requests under one key together, so the report cannot tell the two causes apart.

summary.text: Fences text Evie did not author, such as web pages, transcripts, stored tool output and child agents' reports, so it reads as data rather than instructions.

does.text: Escape puts a backslash before every occurrence of each marker prefix in the data; escaping prefixes rather than exact markers also neutralizes guessed numbered or relabelled variants.
Delimiters numbers the begin and end markers (#1, #2 and so on) until neither occurs in the data, so the closing marker never appears inside the payload.
Frame escapes the text and wraps it between a begin line built from a prefix and a label and a matching end line, numbered as Delimiters requires.

owns.text: Owns no state and no data: it is three pure string functions.

interfaces.text: Callers choose their own marker prefixes and labels: web content, research, explore and build child output, verification output, MCP results, workflow output and assignment data each have their own.
The tools package wraps it as escapeFrameDelimiters and collisionSafeFrame for its own frames.

gotchas.text: A frame labels text, it does not sanitize it: the model still reads the content, and only the frame and the reader's instructions say it is not authority.
It imports only the standard library, so tools, delegation, plugins and subagents share one implementation without import cycles.
A label must not carry untrusted text: delegation labels child output only with the harness-generated execution ID.

summary.text: Loads a Workspace folder's root AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md when AGENTS.md is absent, as bounded repository guidance, and renders it for the model.

does.text: Load returns a snapshot whose status is disabled, unattached, missing, loaded or error, with the file name, exact text and SHA-256 when loaded.
Reads only AGENTS.md, then CLAUDE.md, at the folder's root; it never looks above the root, in subfolders, or at files the guidance mentions.
Refuses symlinks, non-regular files, files over 32 KiB, and text that is not UTF-8 or contains NUL bytes, as visible errors rather than truncating or skipping.
Opens the folder one path component at a time and compares file identities after each open, so a symlink swapped in during the walk cannot redirect the read.

Render wraps loaded text as JSON with its folder and file, after a fixed preface saying the owner's explicit request takes precedence and the guidance cannot change runtime policy, tool permissions, approval requirements or memory scope.

owns.text: Owns no storage: eviedb captures the snapshot once per root user turn in repository_instruction_snapshots, and every iteration and retry of that turn reuses it.

interfaces.text: Load(WorkspaceID, WorkspaceFolder, RepositoryInstructionSettings) and Render(snapshot) are the whole surface; the snapshot type itself belongs to memory.
The agent loop asks the history for the turn's snapshot and places Render's text in its own user-role message after the system prompt and the working-folder note.

gotchas.text: An error status stops an enabled turn before any provider call and leaves a durable turn_failed record; a missing file is normal and adds nothing.
Delegated workers never receive repository instructions: the loop skips them for a session with worker instructions.
If the Workspace folder changes between the snapshot and the turn, the turn fails rather than apply another folder's guidance.
The setting is per Workspace and on by default; turning it off records a disabled snapshot rather than nothing.
Since October 12, 2026 the web UI has no per-turn control, so a turn's stored snapshot is no longer reachable from the browser even though it is still captured.

summary.text: Loads, validates, hashes, reviews and simulates reviewed Workflow Definitions, and supplies the pure step semantics the Workflow Runtime executes; it imports no other Evie package and stores nothing.

does.text: Parses workflow.yaml with gopkg.in/yaml.v3 into the closed Definition schema and accepts only a safe YAML subset: anchors, aliases, merge keys, explicit tags, duplicate keys, nulls, YAML 1.1 booleans and silent number or date conversions are refused with their line, so the reviewed text means exactly one thing.

Validate reads a definition directory through a Source and checks it against an Environment (the capability catalog, the Workspace's access and the operator's worker ceiling); it returns every problem with its definition path, or a Validated value holding the executable hash and the review report.

Validation requires a README.md beside workflow.yaml, schema_version 1, every run limit and a retention classification, and rejects cycles (v1 graphs are acyclic; retries are per step) and steps unreachable from start.

Deterministic steps call only reviewed functions compiled into Evie, named with a version such as collect_claims@1; a definition cannot add one, and each is pure, so the same arguments give the same result.

Computes the executable hash, a SHA-256 over one canonical document (format evie.workflow.executable/1) holding the normalized definition with defaults applied and descriptions left out, the digests of the referenced prompts and schemas, and the identities of the referenced functions; README.md, comments, quoting and formatting never reach it.

Builds the review Report a reviewer reads (the human graph, inputs and outputs, the Run Key rule, capabilities, workers, functions, resources, Retry Policies, Model Policies, requested authority, schedule, retention, limits, the worst-case bounds and warnings) and the ReviewDiff between two versions that the approval card shows.

RequirementsOf extracts what one approval binds besides the executable hash, including the authority hash, and AuthorityOutside lists requested operations the Workspace's current access does not cover.

Simulate dry-runs a definition over fixtures with every external effect replaced by a preview; fixtures supply AI outputs, worker results, capability read results and answers, so a dry run reaches no model, worker or capability provider and never becomes an Effect Receipt.

Supplies the runtime's pure execution helpers (the step graph, accepted run inputs, the Run Key, each step's resolved input, deterministic function calls, branch decisions and the run's outputs); the simulator uses the same helpers, so a run and its dry run cannot disagree about semantics.

Plans map and agent steps: a map's bounds, failure policy and item step over a list a prior step produced, and an agent step's worker preset, Model Policy, reviewed objective, budget and typed result, taken from the worker report's last ## Result block.

Computes Workflow Schedule slots on the schedule's IANA timezone wall clock: a wall time skipped by daylight saving is due when the gap ends and marked shifted, a repeated one is due once at its first occurrence, and $schedule.date and $schedule.time carry the slot's nominal local date and time into the run's inputs.

Decides from the definition alone whether a Successor Run can resume a predecessor's state under a newer version (PlanResume), and which fields a version classifies as sensitive for masking and redaction.

Embeds the bundled definitions (today only deep-research) and owns QualifyBuiltin, the rule a built-in or Global definition must meet: no capability steps, no requested Standing Authority, no schedule, and only the read-only research and explore workers.

owns.text: The closed workflow.yaml schema: a Definition with its typed inputs, Run Key rule, Model Policies, limits, requested authority, schedule, retention classification, start step, steps and outputs, at schema version 1.
The seven step kinds: deterministic, capability, ai, branch, interrupt, map and agent (map and agent were added by the 2026-10-04 amendment).
The schema's hard bounds, such as at most 168 hours per run, 5 attempts per step, a 10-minute backoff, 1,000 map items, 1,000 calls of one operation per run and 31 catch-up runs.
The reviewed registry of deterministic functions, keyed by name@version, compiled into Evie.
The embedded built-in definition files under internal/workflow/builtin, each with the dry-run fixtures its customized copy is proposed with.
No persistent state: it does not run workflows, and activation, runs, leases and effects belong to the runtime and its store.

interfaces.text: Validate(src Source, env Environment) is the entry point; the returned Validated exposes Hash, Report, Files, Name, Simulate and the execution helpers the runtime calls.
Source (ReadFile) is how a definition is read: DirSource for a local directory, procedural.Source for one directory at an exact commit, and an embedded file system for the built-ins.
Catalog is the set of capability contracts a definition validates against; the CLI and the runtime implement it over the Plugin Manager's compiled workflow capabilities.
EncodeValue and DecodeValue are the canonical JSON in which the runtime records accepted inputs, step outputs and checkpoint state.

gotchas.text: ADR 0019 and the spec let an AI Node receive explicitly requested scoped memory, but references have only the $inputs, $steps, $item and $schedule roots and the runtime sends an AI step only its prompt and declared input, so no step can request memory today.

ADR 0008 and the glossary bound Standing Authority by accounts, recipients and limits, but an Operation declares only a capability, a connection, exact resources and max_calls_per_run: resources stand in for recipients, and amounts are not in the schema yet.
The Run Key is the workflow name plus a digest of only the inputs the run_key rule names, so inputs outside the rule never distinguish two logical executions.

Because README.md and description fields are outside the executable hash, editing them never needs a new approval; the change is still committed to procedural Git and recorded against the active version.
Prompts are static Markdown with no templating: an AI step's declared input reaches the model as separate data in the user message, never spliced into the reviewed prompt.

Missed slots are scanned at most 400 days back and the next slot is looked for at most eight years ahead, so a longer outage finds only the bounded window and an impossible date such as 31 February never comes.
Schedules need a named IANA timezone (an empty one or Local is refused), and the package embeds time/tzdata so every host computes slots from the same timezone database.

summary.text: The Workflow Runtime's single entry point: it proposes and activates reviewed definitions, starts Workflow Runs for the owner, a chat or a schedule, and advances them under fenced leases through checkpoints, interruptions and the durable effect protocol.

does.text: Propose validates a definition against the Workspace's current access, simulates it with any fixtures, commits exactly its reviewed files to procedural Git, validates the commit again (its hash must match), and records the proposal with its report and dry run; nothing is activated.

The approval card compares the proposal with the current version (the review diff and the Git patch), lists why approval would be refused now, and gives the exact approve command with both hashes and the expected version.

Approve re-validates the proposal's exact commit and records the owner's approval, which the store checks again in one transaction (the hashes, a dry run that succeeded, the expected version, worker allowances and authority within access); it activates the version and any schedule it declares, and starts no run.

StartRun resolves the version to pin (the Workspace's approved version, else a Global one, else an enabled built-in), re-reads and re-hashes its approved commit, refuses step kinds it cannot run, accepts the input, derives the Run Key and pins the Execution Composition; the store then records the run with its first checkpoint, or returns the run already holding the key.

A start comes from the owner's CLI or web, from a chat's workflow_start (always detached, origin chat), or from a schedule slot (always detached, origin schedule, inputs taken from the approved schedule and the slot).

Start runs the background scheduler in evie serve and the REPL: every poll (one second by default) lists the due runs and starts a pass for each, at most SchedulerConfig.Workers at once (2 by default, EVIE_WORKFLOW_WORKERS up to 32); the first poll is at start, so every startup is a recovery scan.

Each pass claims the run's fenced lease (30 seconds by default, renewed every third of that), re-checks that the run may continue (a compatible pinned runtime, its pinned providers, run admission, its commit still hashing to its approval) and pauses it visibly when it may not, then advances node by node, reading the run back from SQLite before every step.
It executes seven step kinds: branch decisions and deterministic functions, capability reads and effects, AI steps, interruptions, agent steps and map fan-out.

A failed attempt retries within its step's Retry Policy after the step's backoff, recorded as the run's durable not-before time, so whichever process claims the run next retries from the same checkpoint with the same input.

Effects follow the intent-call-receipt-checkpoint order: after per-node admission an Effect Intent with a stable idempotency key and its Resource Conflict Keys is recorded with the attempt, the lease is checked once more, the provider is called, and its answer is recorded as the Effect Receipt with the output and the next checkpoint in one transaction.

An effect without a provable outcome becomes Outcome Unknown: the run needs reconciliation, a provider that reconciles is asked by lookup or idempotent replay after a settle delay, and otherwise the owner reconciles it with evidence; it is never retried by policy.

AI steps send the exact model of their pinned Model Policy two messages, the reviewed prompt and the declared input framed as data with the output schema, through the Models seam; the OpenRouter adapter is wired only when EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS is on.

Agent steps run an existing research, explore or build worker through the Kernel subagent supervisor under the run's lease, with the step's Model Policy and budget; the worker's result is the step's output.
An interrupt step records a typed question and the run waits for the owner holding no lease; Answer validates the reply against the step's schema before the run continues.
Cancel records the owner's cancellation at once: no further node starts, an effect in flight completes or is reconciled first, and the holder then ends the run cancelled with its Run Key free.
The schedule ticker decides due Workflow Schedule slots under one cross-process runner lease and starts them through the same start path with surface schedule.
Every process enforces the operator's daily cap on all runs' AI calls and worker starts (10,000,000 tokens and $5 per UTC day by default); a refused call pauses its run until the next 00:00 UTC.
Migrate creates a Successor Run under a newer approved version when the predecessor's state is valid there, keeping its Run Key, schedule slot, Effect Receipts and what it already used of its limits.

The retention sweep runs hourly under its own runner lease and on the owner's command, applying each classification's policy: mask finished runs' sensitive values on the owner's surfaces, compact checkpoints after seven days, and redact or delete only when configured.

Before the first run pins a built-in version, the runtime commits its embedded files to procedural Git at builtin/workflows/<name> and records the version, so built-in runs read their pinned commit like any approved version.
It implements the Workflows plugin's WorkflowSessions seam, so a chat can start its Workspace's active workflows and read their status.
It lists and marks Durable Notifications and reports today's spend against the daily cap.

owns.text: No tables of its own: every durable record goes through its consumer-owned Store interface, which eviedb's Store implements with the workflow tables for proposals, activations, runs, checkpoints, node attempts, leases, effects, interruptions, schedules, notifications, migrations and retention.

The Execution Composition each run pins as JSON: the runtime version (evie.workflow.runtime/6 today), its step kinds and functions, the pinned capability providers, the Model Policies, and the worker presets with the digest of their composition at start.
The list of pinned runtime versions it declares it can continue, evie.workflow.runtime/1 through /6; a run pinned to any other pauses visibly rather than being reinterpreted.

Only per-process scheduling state lives in memory (the runs this process is advancing, cancellation signals, a schedule-yield time, the built-in cache); each pass reads the run back from SQLite, so any process can continue it from its last checkpoint.
Its holder name, evie-<pid>-<uuid>, which it takes every run lease under and records on every schedule slot it decides.

interfaces.text: New(Config) builds a Runtime from the store, the procedural repository, the capability providers, the operator's worker ceiling, scheduler settings, the model and worker providers, the daily cap and the retention policy; it touches neither Git nor the database.

Owner operations (Propose, Card, Approve, Deactivate, StartRun, InspectRun, ListRuns, Cancel, Answer, Reconcile, Substitute, Schedules, ControlSchedule, Migrate, Sweep, Notifications) are called by the CLI and the web management API; Propose, Approve, Deactivate, Cancel, Answer, Reconcile, Substitute, ControlSchedule, Migrate and Sweep accept only the cli and web surfaces, and StartRun takes a chat or schedule start only through their own paths.

Store is the consumer-owned persistence seam; every run write in it is fenced by the run's current lease, so only the holder of an unexpired lease can begin or finish an attempt, write a checkpoint or fail the run.
CapabilityProviders (WorkflowContract and ResolveWorkflowCapability) is the capability seam the Plugin Manager implements; ContractsOnly gives validation contracts with no providers.
Models (Complete and Pricing) is the AI step provider seam, with NewOpenRouterModels as its production adapter.
Agents runs agent steps' workers; cmd/evie passes the Kernel subagent supervisor.
StartFromChat, ChatRunStatus and ChatWorkflows implement plugins.WorkflowSessions for the Workflows plugin's workflow_start and workflow_status tools.
Start(ctx) returns a stop function that ends every pass between nodes, releases the leases and waits at most five seconds.

gotchas.text: ADR 0005 and user story 1 have a workflow proposed and reviewed in an Evie session, but Propose accepts only the owner's cli or web surface, the web management API offers no proposal route (proposals come from the CLI), and a chat cannot propose.

ADR 0017 says revoked Standing Authority pauses active runs before their next covered effect; the code applies run admission in the transaction that records every node attempt, so a deactivation, block or revocation pauses a run at its very next node of any kind.
ADR 0045 says each Workspace may define retention and export rules, but retention is the operator's policy per classification read from the environment; Workspace rules and export are a follow-up.

ADR 0021 says Evie rejects a second active run; the code does not refuse a duplicate start but returns the run already holding the Run Key (Existing is true), and failed, cancelled and superseded runs free the key for a new start.
ADR 0046 speaks of Background Runs, but a trigger on workflow_runs records a Durable Notification for every run's terminal or needs-attention transition, foreground CLI starts included.
A foreground start executes the run inline in the caller's process when no scheduler runs there, detached from the caller's cancellation: a caller that stops waiting never stops the run.
A detached start from a one-shot evie workflows command only records the run; a running evie serve or REPL executes it.

AI and agent steps are off unless EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS is on with an OpenRouter key: a start of a definition that needs them is refused, and a run that reaches one in an Evie without them pauses until an Evie that allows them claims it.

While any Effect Intent of a run has no receipt, no node starts and the run is never paused, resumed or failed; that wait still counts toward limits.max_duration, while waits for an answer or at the daily cap do not.

A node interrupted three times at one checkpoint (its runtime crashed, stopped or lost the lease before recording the outcome) fails the run instead of running again; interrupted effect attempts do not count, since their outcome was reconciled.
Stopping waits at most five seconds; a pass still inside a node keeps its lease until it expires, and the next claim records that attempt interrupted, or its effect's outcome unknown.

An effect's idempotency key derives from the Workspace, the Run Key, the step, the capability, connection, resource and input, so a later run of the same logical execution reuses it; only the owner's rerun override changes the Run Key, and with it every key.

Resource Conflict Keys are scoped only by connection and held across every run and Workspace, so two Workspaces sharing a connection serialize their writes, and max_calls_per_run counts every Effect Intent, retries and a predecessor's intents included.
A run paused at the daily cap is rechecked only at the next 00:00 UTC; raising the cap during the day helps new calls at once but not that run.

summary.text: The explicit, non-overlapping states a Workflow Run moves through; succeeded, failed, cancelled and superseded are terminal and their history is never rewritten.

transitions.label: an interrupt step asks before any attempt
paused at its claim (provider, admission, models or workers unavailable)
fails between attempts (a run limit or an unreadable checkpoint)
the attempt that ends the graph records the run's outputs
an attempt fails with no retry left, or a run limit is reached
an interrupt step records its question
paused: provider unavailable, admission refused, Resource Conflict Key held, or the daily cap reached
resumed at a claim once its cause is gone and no effect is unresolved
a receipt from the provider's or the owner's reconciliation
the owner cancels; it finishes once the effect has its receipt
nothing in flight and every effect has its receipt; open questions are withdrawn
the owner migrates it to a Successor Run
the owner migrates it once no lease holds it
the owner migrates a paused run

summary.text: Every node attempt is recorded running before the node runs and finished exactly once; a finished attempt is immutable, and a retry is a new attempt from the same checkpoint.

transitions.label: its output is recorded with the next checkpoint in one transaction
its error is recorded; retried after the backoff or the run fails; an effect whose outcome became unknown also ends failed
its holder stopped before recording the outcome: the next claim, or the holder itself while stopping, records it

summary.text: An Effect Intent's state is derived from its immutable records: pending until a receipt or an unknown outcome is recorded, and settled only by an Effect Receipt.

transitions.label: the provider's response is recorded as the receipt
no answer in time, a panic, a malformed response, an unproven error, or the holder stopped
reconciled as happened, by the provider's lookup or the owner's evidence

summary.text: Evie's procedural Git repository: a private bare repository at ~/.evie/procedural, written only with Git plumbing, that holds proposed and approved Workflow Definitions at exact commits; Git answers what was proposed and approved, while SQLite owns approval records and runs.

does.text: New touches nothing; the repository is created on first use with mode 0700 and git init --bare on branch master, and a root that is a link, a file or not Evie's bare repository is refused.

Commit makes one commit on master whose tree is master's with one directory replaced by exactly the given files, built with hash-object, mktree and commit-tree; it makes no commit when the tree would not change.

Master moves only by a compare-and-swap update-ref, retried on top of a concurrent writer's commit up to 32 times, so no writer's commit is lost and a crash before the ref moves leaves only unreferenced objects.
ReadFile reads one regular file at an exact commit, refusing anything that is not a full commit hash, a clean relative path or a file of at most 1 MiB.
Source returns a workflow Source reading one directory at one commit, so validation at approval and at every run start reads exactly the approved files.
Diff gives the patch of a directory between two commits (or from nothing) for the approval card, truncated at 512 KiB.

owns.text: The bare repository at ~/.evie/procedural and its single branch, master.

The tree its callers lay out: workspaces/<id>/workflows/<name> for Workspace definitions, global/workflows/<name> for Global ones, builtin/workflows/<name> for recorded built-in versions and global/skills/<name> for proposed and approved skills.
Commit messages that carry the definition's Executable-Hash and Authority-Hash, written by Evie's own identity.

interfaces.text: *Repo with Head, Commit, ReadFile, Source, Diff and Root; the Workflow Runtime receives one through Config.Repo, and cmd/evie builds it at the default root.
Source satisfies the workflow package's Source interface (ReadFile by slash path relative to the definition's directory).

gotchas.text: It shells out to the git binary: every command runs with a built environment (only PATH and HOME inherited, no global or system configuration), hardening flags that turn off hooks, fsmonitor, signing, maintenance and transports, and a two-second wait delay.
Every file tool refuses ~/.evie/procedural, so no worker or chat can read or write the reviewed definitions behind the runtime's back.
Readers always name an exact commit, so a later commit never changes what an earlier approval or run reads; there is no work tree to leave dirty.

ADR 0012 also plans user-authored Agent Presets as reviewed assets in procedural Git, but no code stores presets here: presets are compiled into the plugins package, and only cmd/evie and workflowruntime use this repository.

summary.text: Checks one skill in the Agent Skills format against Evie's rules (no scripts, executables or links; only UTF-8 text within the size limits; a valid name and description) and identifies each version by the SHA-256 of its canonical manifest.

does.text: ReadFolder checks every entry of a skill folder with Lstat through an os.Root before anything is read or committed, refusing links inside the folder, a scripts/ folder at any depth, executable and non-regular files, skipping operating-system and version-control clutter (.DS_Store, ._ files, Icon\r, .git) with a warning, and stopping at 64 files or 1 MiB; only a folder that is itself a link is followed.

Parse refuses a missing or invalid name or description, a name unlike its folder or clashing with /compact or /model, and files that are not UTF-8, hold a NUL byte or exceed 32 KiB; it reads Claude Code's unquoted argument-hint as its raw text, and warns about frontmatter Evie ignores, shell commands and blocks, argument placeholders and mentions of Claude Code tools, never running or substituting any of them.
ReadVersion reads a version back from where it was stored, such as one procedural commit, and requires it to check and hash exactly as recorded.
Pinned is an approved version a chat pins in its Composition Receipt as skill.global.<name> with its version hash; its Source reads the version's folder at the procedural commit it was approved at.
Catalog renders the framed catalog message of a chat's model-invocable skills, each name with its description, keeping every name and shortening the longest descriptions evenly to fit 8 KiB.

Body and File render a pinned version's instructions and resource list, or one of its files, in the owner-approved-guidance frame, reading only files its manifest lists and checking each against its hash; MaxLoadBytes bounds what they return, so a loaded skill is always shown whole.

summary.text: Evie's Kernel persistence: it opens and upgrades ~/.evie/evie.db and is the one Store through which conversations, Semantic Memory and its review, Tasks, Workspaces, Workflow Runs, subagents, MCP connection records and Changes are written, each under its own transaction and fencing rules.

does.text: Startup and migrations: every open forces the file to mode 0600, retries only SQLite BUSY while pinging for up to five seconds, runs the base schema, then thirty upgrade steps in a fixed order, from Workspaces, workflows, MCP and subagents through Semantic Memory, the compiler and its review, retrieval and the background pass to plugins, Tasks and session titles, with a check of the Semantic Memory projection among them.

Transactions: writes that must not interleave run through withImmediateTransaction, which takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE on a dedicated connection, resolves COMMIT and ROLLBACK under a context that ignores caller cancellation but keeps its deadline, and discards a connection whose rollback failed instead of returning it to the pool.

Sessions: creates Global, project and Workspace sessions together with their Composition Receipt, creates delegated child sessions that inherit the parent's Context Scope, and archives an idle owner session by closing it, which is refused while its turn lease or a child subagent is live.

Episodic Memory: AppendEventWithLease checks the holder's fencing token and appends the event in one immediate transaction, giving it the next per-session sequence, validating terminal, snapshot and compaction correlations, titling the session from its first owner message, and projecting the event into the conversation index and session episodes in the same transaction.

Turn leases: acquiring a session's lease succeeds only when no unexpired holder exists, bumps the fencing token and generation, can require the chat's current model revision, and first releases that session's inactive Task Claims; SessionTurnOwner binds acquire, heartbeat, authorize and release to one holder for the agent.

Semantic Memory kernel: every change is a Prepare/Apply pair (remember a literal or an Entity, correct, retire or restore, link, promote, classify as standing); Prepare resolves the request against SQLite (for a remember, the exact cited owner event) and returns an immutable proposal without writing, and Apply takes the turn lease, revalidates, and commits the Semantic Operation with its projection rows, provenance, state event and Scope Revision atomically.

Replay: accepted operations are the canonical history; VerifySemanticProjection replays them into a disposable shadow projection and quarantines the scopes that disagree, OwnerRebuildSemanticProjection swaps a verified shadow in under a fenced maintenance lock, and startup checks only cheap revision and frontier invariants.

Memory reads: answers exact Claim inspection, the memory overview and standing set, graph neighbourhood traversal and the archived-session audit, each bound to one Scope Context: the reader's own, or for the audit the closed session's.

Retrieval: SearchMemory treats full-text, exact and alias matches and optional dense vectors as suggestions and re-reads every returned Claim from accepted state inside one read-only transaction with a 500 ms deadline; Conversation Excerpts, conversation expansion and session-episode search have their own bounded reads.

Index maintenance: retrieval indexes trail accepted state through generations, checkpoints and dirty queues that triggers fill inside the accepting transaction; RefreshMemoryIndex shares one batch of at most 256 rows between the accepted-Claim, conversation and dense indexes, and dense embedding runs only when EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on and EVIE_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT is set.

Proposal inbox and background pass: queues proactive memory proposals exactly as prepared and applies one only on the owner's approval; stores the background pass's activation (also its cross-process runner lease), per-conversation cursors and run records, and commits a pass's proposals with its cursor in one transaction fenced by the conversation's turn lease.

Memory compiler: CompileCandidateUnit and QueueCandidateUnit seal one bounded source unit into a job under a Compiler Generation, history backfill seals source coordinates for later work, and RunCompilerHost reconciles those obligations and drives extraction through a CompilerExtractor; what it produces is Memory Candidates, never accepted memory.
