Candidate review: LocalOwnerReviewContext mints an HMAC-sealed review capability bound to one scope and the stored key's revision, and every review read and write re-checks it in its own transaction before preparing, editing, choosing an identity or a time, batching, or resolving a candidate.

Workflows: it is the Workflow Runtime's authoritative record: proposals and activations bound to exact hashes and Workspace Access revisions, runs pinned at start with immutable checkpoints and node attempts, fenced run leases with takeover history, Effect Intents and Receipts with Outcome Unknown, interruptions, AI and worker calls, schedules and their slots, notifications, cancellation, migration and retention.

Cross-process arbitration: the workflow schedule ticker, the retention sweep and the background memory pass each take a single runner lease stored in the database, so serve, the REPL and a CLI run sharing one file do not do the same work twice.

Tasks: stores Tasks and Task Trees with revisions, idempotent mutations and decomposition, Task Claims tied to a session's turn lease, Task Access Grants for delegated children, dependency-aware readiness, and the one-time import of the legacy ~/.todo/DayToDay.json list.

Workspaces: registers Workspaces whose preset choices and research, explore and build allowances belong to immutable Workspace Revisions, while Workspace Access, the folder, repository-instruction settings, verify commands and MCP tool policies each keep their own append-only revisions; every change is a compare-and-set on the expected revision.
Workspace tabs: records the owner's approval of each tab's data list by its key, so a changed list needs approval again, and keeps each tab's recent problems.

Subagents: records every subagent attempt in one execution table, from admission against the parent's lease and policy caps through the running edge only one caller wins, finish states and continuations, to build workers' pinned worktrees and merge-gate steps, run-owned workers for workflow agent steps, reports, and recovery of attempts whose process died.

MCP connections: stores each connection's record, status and OAuth metadata but never its credentials, which the Keychain holds, and each session's pinned Workspace Access revision, which mcpchat intersects with the current access to decide the MCP tools a chat may reach.

Changes and build verification: Evie's own Changes are derived from build attempts with nothing new stored, a GitHub Repository's pull requests are kept as the last sync saw them along with the owner's 'merge when checks pass' arms, Change notices go into the notifications store, and BuildVerifyFor gives the merge gate a Workspace's or project's setup and verify commands.

Repository instructions: captures a Workspace's instructions once per root turn as an immutable snapshot, reading the folder's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md outside the write transaction and re-checking the folder and settings revisions under the turn lease before storing it.

Plugins and composition: seeds each compiled plugin's enabled default once and keeps the owner's later choice, and stores each session's Composition Receipt and the Compatibility Resolutions recorded when it resumes.

Owner diagnostics: ReadConversationUsage selects only the usage counters and requested model of assistant events, never their text, and the database browser returns schema topology for every table but row records only for the cron tables, refusing events and semantic tables (typed views only) and everything else.

owns.text: Episodic Memory: sessions and their append-only events, plus each session's model setting, turn lease, Composition Receipt, Compatibility Resolutions, Task Focus and pinned Workspace Access.

Projects and Workspaces: the projects and workspaces rows and the revision tables for presets and their revocations, folders, instruction settings, explore and build allowances, verify commands and Workspace Access, plus tab data approvals and tab problems.

Semantic Memory (17 semantic_* tables): the accepted-operation log with its per-scope revisions, and the projection of scopes, Entities, Aliases, versioned Predicates, Claims, corrections, classifications, Source Links, Graph Links, state events and Promotions, plus quarantine and maintenance-lock state.

Derived retrieval state, which is never memory: FTS5 tables for accepted Claims and for conversation messages with their id-to-rowid lookups, dirty queues and generation checkpoints, dense vector tables for Claims and events, and session episodes with their own full-text table.
The background pass and the proposal inbox: one activation row, a cursor per root conversation, one row per pass, and the queued proposals with the owner's declines.

The memory compiler (43 memory_compiler_* tables): generations, sealed jobs and their schedule, selections, candidates and candidate groups, coverage, per-conversation activations, history backfill requests, diagnostics, recurrence links, status projections, capacity and release receipts.
Candidate review (12 memory_review_* tables): the review authentication key, previews and deliveries, resolutions and audits, batch previews, and the edit, identity, temporal and inbox revisions.

Tasks (the tasks table and 19 task_* tables): hierarchy, events, revisions, claims and claim events, access and event grants, idempotency and mutation results, decomposition and coordination records, and legacy Todo import provenance.

Workflows (33 workflow_* tables): Workspace and Global proposals, activations and deactivations, built-in versions and controls, runs with checkpoints, node attempts, leases and recovery events, Effect Intents, Receipts, unknowns and conflicts, interruptions, model and worker calls, schedule slots and controls, notifications, cancellations, overrides, migrations, substitutions and retention state.
Subagents: one subagent_executions row per attempt, which also carries a build worker's worktree and merge-gate record.
MCP and Changes: MCP connection records and per-Workspace tool policies, and a Repository's synced pull requests and merge arms.
Repository instruction snapshots, keyed by session and root turn and immutable by trigger.
Plugin enabled configuration, and the cron tables jobs and job_runs, whose schema lives here though the cron tools and `evie cron-exec` read and write them directly.

interfaces.text: Opening: OpenDB and OpenDBContext open ~/.evie/evie.db, creating ~/.evie with mode 0700; OpenDBAt and OpenDBAtContext open any path with the same upgrades (tests and the explorer tool use them); OpenDBReadOnlyContext opens with mode=ro and no upgrades, for query_db.
NewStore wraps the *sql.DB; UseClock replaces the clock and the owner's time zone before the Store is shared, so a deterministic evaluation can replay history on a synthetic timeline.

The Store is concrete; it and its bound views satisfy interfaces their consumers own, such as the agent's History (through SessionHistory) and SemanticGraphMemory, mcpconn.Records, usage.ConversationReader, web's CandidateReviewKernel and DatabaseInspector, and the small per-command kernel interfaces in cmd/evie.
BindHistory and BindTurnOwner give one agent session views bound to its session and lease holder, so every append it makes carries that holder's lease.
Fenced writes take a TurnLease or a WorkflowRunLease, and the lease writer is package-private, so no caller can pass its own SQL into a fenced transaction.
Sentinel errors are part of the contract, such as ErrTurnLeaseHeld, ErrSessionModelChanged, ErrWorkspaceNotFound and ErrOwnerReviewUnauthorized, which web maps to status codes and messages.

Kernel-only seams stay off model-facing interfaces: ManagementUpdateGlobalTask, IssueTaskAccessGrant, OwnerRebuildSemanticProjection and LocalOwnerReviewContext are called by trusted hosts, never through task.Service or a tool.
Long-running entry points for the hosts in cmd/evie: RunCompilerHost(ctx, CompilerSupervisorConfig) for the compiler host and RefreshMemoryIndex(ctx, limit) for each retrieval maintenance batch.

gotchas.text: There is no schema version number: every open re-runs CREATE IF NOT EXISTS and each upgrade step inspects the live schema (a column's presence, a table's SQL) to decide whether it applies, so any process that opens the file migrates it.

The startup retry covers only the first ping, when concurrent fresh processes can get BUSY enabling WAL; schema statements are never retried, and the pinned driver's connection setup cannot be interrupted by the five-second budget.
Events refuse UPDATE and DELETE by trigger, and Hard Erasure is not implemented (memory changes are reversible Retirement), so no Store path removes conversation evidence.
The package is not pure SQL: dense maintenance calls the local embedding endpoint, repository-instruction capture reads the Workspace folder, and the legacy Todo import reads ~/.todo/DayToDay.json.

Dense indexing follows the environment of whichever process runs maintenance: one without EVIE_REMOTE_MEMORY=on and an embedding endpoint disables the dense selection on its next tick, and the next process that has them re-enables it from checkpoint zero, re-embedding everything.

Index names carry each index's own generation, not one schema version: memory_retrieval_fts_v3 holds accepted Claims (accepted-fts-unicode61-v3), while conversation messages live in memory_retrieval_event_fts_v4.
workflow_notifications is the general Durable Notification store despite its name: Change notices land there too, with an empty workflow and a change_id.
LocalOwnerReviewContext says web callers must call it only after owner authentication, but web's only check is the loopback guard; there are no user accounts, so the guard is the whole owner check.

Per-conversation compiler activation is still implemented here (ActivateCompiler, ResumeCompilerActivation), but nothing outside tests calls it since the background pass replaced it; existing activations can only be read and disabled.
The package has no package comment, so its extracted doc is empty; the closest overview is the Store type and the open path in db.go.

summary.text: The HTTP surface of `evie serve`: one loopback ServeMux that serves the embedded React app, streams chat turns as server-sent events, holds open chats and pending approvals in memory, and exposes the owner's surfaces as JSON routes behind a cross-origin guard.

does.text: Route table and guards: POST /api/chat and POST /api/approve sit behind guard; six routes have no wrapper: /, the OAuth callback, the two GET /workspace-tabs routes, and /explorer and /explorer/, the System page, served outside the API guard by decision; every other route sits behind managementRoute (guard plus POST-only).

guard admits a request only when its Content-Type is exactly application/json, its Origin (if any) names a loopback host and its Host is loopback, answering 403 otherwise; managementRoute answers 405 with Allow: POST to any other method before guard runs.
listenAddr resolves EVIE_ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:6687) and refuses any host that is not loopback, because there is no authentication: the loopback bind and the guard are the whole boundary.

Routes exist only when their seam is wired: constructor arguments and With* options set fields, and each register function returns early when its field is nil or the controller lacks an optional interface, so one Handler serves both the full and the management-only server.

Chat turns: POST /api/chat runs a turn in the chat the request names, streamed as SSE in the response or, with detach, answered 202 at once and streamed through the chat's feed; it is refused with 409 when that chat is not open, already running a turn or changed model, and 503 when the server has no chat.

A turn runs on the runtime context, not the request's, so closing the browser never cancels it; only POST /api/cancel stops the named chat's turn, and /api/compact runs the agent's manual compaction for that chat.

Open chats: keeps up to eight chats open, each with its own agent session and model revision, closing the least recently used idle chat to make room; each chat's live feed replays the running turn's events to a tab that joins late, and chat status streams which chats run or wait on an approval.

Approvals: holds the pending-approval map and the two approvers (the streaming request's and the detached turn's followed one); the full exchange is the approval handshake flow among the agent loop's flows.

Context sessions: lists Workspaces, projects and sessions, opens or creates the selected Global, project or Workspace session through the ContextSessionController, returns its history, archives and restores chats and Workspaces, and switches a chat's model.

Workspace surfaces: files and diffs from the attached folder, terminals in that folder (at most eight, each living as long as its streaming request), the Workspace's own tabs with their approved data reads (at most four at once across Evie), Repository and GitHub status, Changes with push, merge and sync, and subagent traces.

Memory surfaces: Semantic Memory scopes, objects and inspection in the focused chat's scope, evidence behind a recall, compiler candidate review (single, batch, edit, identity, time) with diagnostics, the proposal inbox, and the background pass's status.

Data hub and workflows: database schema and allowlisted rows, usage and spending summaries, and the Workflow Runtime's list, review, approve, start, runs, answers, reconciliation, cancellation, schedules, notifications, retention and built-ins.
MCP: lists, adds, connects, waits on and disconnects MCP connections for serve's connection manager, receives the OAuth callback, and reviews which server tools a Workspace may use.

The folder chooser opens a native macOS panel through osascript on the server's desktop, so it is the one route that also requires a loopback peer address and an Origin, when present, matching the Host.

Static app: serves the build compiled into the binary, falls back to index.html (no-store, frame-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none') for any path not in the build, and caches fingerprinted assets for a year.

Lifecycle: ServeWithContext listens, logs the URL and serves until the context ends, then gives the HTTP server five seconds to shut down; Close drains the folder picker and terminals and waits up to ten seconds for detached turns to record how they ended.

owns.text: Only per-process state: open chats, their feeds and replay buffers, pending approvals and the chat each belongs to, each running turn's stop control, terminals and the folder picker; nothing here survives a restart.

No tables: durable reads and writes go through the seams it is handed, mostly *eviedb.Store, which serve passes as the receipt inspector, Semantic Memory, database inspector, candidate review and subagent reader.
Embedded assets: the built UI under ui/dist and, for Workspace tabs, Evie's helper script and the prelude that every tab page starts with.

Request limits: a management body is one JSON value of at most 4 KiB with unknown fields refused, unless its route sets its own limit. Candidate review takes 8 KiB, except resolve and batch/resolve (32 KiB), batch/prepare (64 KiB) and edit (264 KiB); the compiler diagnostics, proposal inbox and background status routes decode as candidate review does, at 8 KiB; and a Workspace tab's approve and data requests take 32 KiB.

interfaces.text: ServeWithContext(ctx, server) is the entry point cmd/evie calls; Handler() returns the mux so tests drive it through httptest with no port and no model.

Constructors layer seams: NewServer, NewManagedServer (plugins and receipts), NewContextServer (context sessions), NewContextMemoryServer (Semantic Memory) and NewContextDataServer (database inspection).
With* options add one surface each: candidate review, background status, usage, spending, workflows, repositories, Changes, change sync, push, merge, subagents, MCP connections and MCP tool review.

Its seams are interfaces it owns, such as ContextSessionController (implemented by cmd/evie's webContextSessionController), ReceiptInspector, DatabaseInspector, UsageReader, WorkflowManager and MCPConnections.
sseEvents implements the agent's Events contract and writes each event as one SSE block, the web twin of the REPL's terminal output.

gotchas.text: Unguarded `/` is safe: it answers only GET and HEAD with files compiled into the binary (or the index.html shell), reads no state and performs no action, and the shell forbids other sites from framing Evie.

Unguarded /api/connections/oauth/callback is unguarded by necessity, since the authorization server's redirect is a cross-site browser navigation; it accepts only GET with a single-use, unexpired state that serve minted, exchanges the code with that attempt's PKCE verifier, and returns an escaped, no-store, no-referrer page.
Unguarded GET /workspace-tabs/{workspace}/{tab} only redirects to the trailing-slash URL, built from IDs that passed their patterns, so it cannot point off Evie and reads nothing.

Unguarded GET /workspace-tabs/{workspace}/{tab}/{path...} is safe because it is sealed rather than guarded: it requires a loopback Host, serves only files of an active Workspace's tab folder, and every response is sandboxed without same-origin, opens no connections and may be framed only by Evie, so a tab's page cannot reach Evie's routes (its Origin is null); WebRTC remains an accepted residual risk.

Comments and the spec say less than the code: Handler's comment says every /api route sits behind the guard and connections.go calls the callback the one unguarded route, and serve.spec.md requires JSON on every /api handler, yet the callback takes plain GET and five other routes are unguarded (/, the two GET /workspace-tabs routes, /explorer and /explorer/); the code is what runs.

guard is a cross-site defence, not authentication: any local process that sends JSON with a loopback Host passes it (the CLI's connection commands rely on that), and /api/chats/follow replays a running turn's approval_request events, ids included, to any such caller, so the id is no secret from local software.

A request to an /api path that is not registered (any route of a seam that was not wired) falls through to the static handler: POST gets 405 'static assets are GET only' and GET gets the app shell with 200, never 404.
POST /api/chat and POST /api/approve decode their bodies with no size limit and accept unknown fields, unlike management routes.
Most route facts show no method because the patterns have none; managementRoute enforces POST inside the handler instead.

serve.spec.md still describes one global session held in memory, with persistence and multiple conversations out of scope, but the server keeps up to eight open chats over durable sessions and serves their history.

Several files carry a comment above `package web`; the extractor takes the first by file name, so the package doc shown is approvals.go's approval-handshake sentence rather than events.go's 'Package web is the evie web frontend'.

summary.text: The map snapshot: a tiny package beside the system map page that builds the page into the evie binary, so the System view shows the Map, Architecture and History of the build that is running.

does.text: Files returns the snapshot rooted at the explorer directory: system.html alone, the self-contained page the vision skill builds from .vision/map.json, fixed when the binary is built.
internal/web serves the page under /explorer/, at the directory and by its own name, GET and HEAD only, with a 404 for anything else.
Every response carries one content-security policy: the page's inline scripts allowed by their hashes, taken once from the snapshot, and inline styles, reaching no host but Evie.

owns.text: No data of its own: only the page as it was in the commit the binary was built from.

interfaces.text: One function, Files, returning an fs.FS; internal/web is its only importer.

gotchas.text: go:embed reaches only its own directory, so this one package lives under docs/ rather than internal/, and the explorer tool's package extraction names its directory explicitly.
An edit to the map reaches evie serve only once the page is rebuilt and the binary with it; the facts, README.md and the Go file itself stay out of the snapshot.

summary.text: The evie binary and Evie's composition root: main loads the environment, dispatches one-shot commands, and otherwise wires the Store, Plugin Manager, subagent supervisor, Workflow Runtime and memory hosts into the terminal REPL or `evie serve`.

does.text: Starts by warming the login-shell environment snapshot in the background and loading ~/.evie/.env, then .env and ../../.env, each in its own call.

Dispatches in a fixed order: cron-exec first; then commands that need no database (workflow review, and the MCP connection commands, which call serve); then it opens the database and offers the arguments to each management handler in turn, every handler answering handled=false for arguments that are not its own.

`evie cron-exec <job-id>` runs one cron job's command under a 30-minute bound and records the run, returning 0 even when the job fails so launchd never treats Evie as broken; it builds no model client.
Memory, Workspace, project, worktree and Change commands run straight against the Store through small interfaces each handler owns, before any plugin or model is wired.

`evie workflows` activation commands build their own subagent supervisor, a narrower Plugin Manager (the workflow capability plugins plus Web, Todo and Subagents) and a Workflow Runtime, run one command, and give the workers five seconds to stop.

For everything else it imports the legacy Todo list, recovers inactive Task Claims and subagent records, builds the subagent supervisor from the EVIE_SUBAGENTS_* limits, and compiles the Plugin Manager from the Kernel toolset and ten First-party Plugins with their default enabled states; `plugins`, `presets` and `sessions` then run on that manager and exit.

With no command it runs the REPL: subagent recovery, the workflow scheduler (or a reason why workflows are unavailable), the session chooser, an agent session against OpenRouter, the memory hosts, and the REPL loop until input closes.

`evie serve` wires usage, spending, the Workflow Runtime and its scheduler, change sync and the merger, MCP connections and their session pool, and then either a management-only server or the full chat server; the `evie serve` startup flow walks it step by step.

Late-bound links let chat tools reach things built later: WorkflowLink is bound to the Workflow Runtime once it starts (or marked unavailable), and MCPLink only in serve, so REPL chats report that MCP tools need serve.

Every agent session is bound to its pinned Composition Receipt: a new session keeps the snapshot it was created with, an existing one resumes from its receipt and records Compatibility Resolutions, and a legacy session without one records the default once.

In serve, webContextSessionController opens web chats: it creates or resumes the selected Global, project or Workspace session (a new Workspace chat uses the Workspace's default preset), binds its composition and builds an agent on the chat's own model.

Owns the long-lived hosts' wiring: the background memory pass (with its own OpenRouter or local model), retrieval maintenance (a batch of up to 256 rows each second, every 100 ms while work is pending, every 5 s after a failure), the optional compiler host from EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG, subagent recovery and change sync; the three memory hosts' stops wait at most five seconds, while recovery and sync stops wait for their loops to end.
One changes.Service reads Workspace Repositories, so Settings, the owner's pushes and workflows' pushes share its folder lock; it reaches GitHub only when GITHUB_TOKEN is set.

owns.text: No tables of its own; durable state goes through eviedb. It owns wiring choices such as each compiled plugin's default enabled state, which is seeded once per database.

The environment settings parsed here: EVIE_MODEL (default agent.DefaultModel), OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, EVIE_ADDR for the connection commands, EVIE_COMPILER_CONFIG, the EVIE_SUBAGENTS_* limits, EVIE_WORKFLOW_WORKERS, EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS, and the workflow daily cap and retention policies.
Checked-in Workspace Workflow Definitions (finance-daily and finance-review) under cmd/evie/workflows, which the owner proposes with `evie workflows propose`; the binary does not embed them.
The feature specs and decision records under cmd/evie/docs, the sources of truth for Evie's active features.

interfaces.text: The CLI itself: `evie` for the REPL, `evie serve`, `evie cron-exec <job-id>` for launchd, and the management commands the panel lists.
Each management handler takes a small kernel interface of its own that *eviedb.Store satisfies, so it can be tested with a fake.
webContextSessionController implements web's ContextSessionController and its optional controllers (archiving, Workspace creation and settings, folders, tabs, repository instructions, models).
The connection commands are an HTTP client of serve: they POST JSON to serve's /api/connections routes at EVIE_ADDR.

gotchas.text: The package comment is stale: it says `serve` will run the web frontend once internal/web exists.
`evie memory-compiler activate` and `resume` are still recognised commands, but they always fail with the retirement message: the background pass replaced per-conversation activation.

serve checks EVIE_ADDR only inside ServeWithContext, after the scheduler, change sync and memory hosts have started; a refused address or a busy port ends the process through log.Fatalf, which skips the deferred stops, so a workflow lease taken in that moment is recovered only when it expires.

Management-only serve passes the server no context-session controller and no Semantic Memory or database seam, so besides chat it lacks Workspaces, folders, terminals, tabs, Changes, models, memory reads and the database browser.
Changing defaultPluginEnabled reaches only databases that never resolved that plugin: the default is seeded once and the owner's stored choice wins.
Serve can hold several OpenRouter clients: the chat client, the background pass's own, and the workflow runtime's for AI and agent steps when EVIE_WORKFLOW_REMOTE_MODELS=on.

summary.text: The `todo` command: the owner's CLI for Evie's durable Task Trees, which opens the Evie database directly and changes Tasks through the same Store rules the chat's Todo tools use.

does.text: run dispatches list, get, add, update, start, block, done, cancel, reopen, delete, release-claim and show, prints the usage for help, and exits 2 for an unknown command or bad flags and 1 for a failure.
Before every command it opens ~/.evie/evie.db (applying its upgrades), imports the legacy Todo list once, and releases Task Claims whose execution is no longer live.
Attributes every change to the local owner and a session: the fixed Global session `todo-cli` without --session, or the named primary session and its Workspace or project.

A status change that needs a Task Claim (start, block, done, a result summary, reopening work in progress, cancelling claimed work) takes the session's turn lease for one minute and a claim, applies the update, then releases both.
Without --revision a lifecycle command uses the Task's current revision, and it generates an idempotency key unless --idempotency-key is given, which then requires --revision.
release-claim is an audited override with a required reason, and delete cancels through the management override with the reason todo_cli_delete, keeping the Task.

show prints a Task Tree's orchestration progress: each Task's status, dependencies, paths, claim (this session, live or stale) and latest build worker, then the Ready Set todo_ready would offer, batches, builds in flight and blocked Tasks with reasons.

owns.text: No tables of its own: it writes the Task tables through eviedb and creates the `todo-cli` session row on first use.
The usage text, which documents every flag, the status values and the rule that flags precede positional arguments.

interfaces.text: The `todo` CLI, its words listed in the panel; main hands os.Args to run(ctx, args, stdout, stderr), which returns the exit code so tests drive it without a process.
It talks only to the Store, through the task package's types; it needs neither serve nor a model.

gotchas.text: todo never loads ~/.evie/.env, and show sizes batches with delegation.DefaultPolicy, so its Ready Set can differ from the chat's todo_ready, which uses the EVIE_SUBAGENTS_* limits.
With --session naming a chat whose turn is running, a claim-needing update fails, because the session's turn lease is held.
Flags must come before positional arguments: Go's flag parsing stops at the first non-flag word.

summary.text: Content-free owner diagnostics for Data > Usage: it reads Codex account activity and local Codex token records and summarizes Evie's own recorded token usage, and none of it becomes conversation evidence, billing authority or runtime budget state.

does.text: ParsePeriod accepts an inclusive from date, an exclusive to date and a non-empty time zone that time.LoadLocation knows (an IANA name, UTC, or Local for the server's own zone), from 1 to 90 calendar days, and refuses a date that the zone would shift.

Summarize totals observations overall, per local day and per model: a missing counter stays unavailable while a reported zero stays zero, every counter carries how many calls reported it, the cached share is weighted over calls with compatible input and cached counts, and inconsistent records count as anomalies.

InspectUsage returns one source per Codex account (merged across homes that share an account), one unassigned local source per Codex home, and Evie's own source, each with its state, coverage and message, so one failing source never hides the others.

ReadCodexAccount runs `codex app-server --stdio` with MCP servers, analytics and apps turned off, CODEX_HOME set and stderr discarded, for at most 20 seconds, and calls only initialize, account/read, account/rateLimits/read and account/usage/read; raw errors are never forwarded.

LocalIndex scans the JSONL files under each home's sessions and archived_sessions in memory, keeping only token metadata and per-file offsets, deduplicating records across copies, and rebuilding from the files when one is removed, replaced or truncated.
Evie's source comes from the Store's ReadConversationUsage, which reads only the usage counters and requested model of accepted assistant events across all sessions.

Configuration: EVIE_CODEX_BIN picks the executable (else the ChatGPT desktop bundle's codex, else codex on PATH), and EVIE_CODEX_HOMES lists up to four absolute homes (else CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex).

owns.text: No tables and no files: only in-memory collector caches per Codex home (the last account snapshot and the local index), which a restart rebuilds.
The usage report shapes: Period, Metrics with exact counters sent as decimal strings, Summary, Source, Account with quota windows, and Report.
The bounds: 90 days per request, 200,000 observations, 10,000 local files and 200 models per summary.

interfaces.text: NewService(ctx, conversations, binary, homes) builds the reader serve hands to web; its background reads live as long as ctx.
Service.InspectUsage(ctx, period) satisfies web's UsageReader, which POST /api/data/usage/summary calls with a from, to and timezone.
ConversationReader is the one interface it owns; the Store implements it, which is why eviedb imports usage and not the reverse.

gotchas.text: Collection runs only when someone asks: InspectUsage starts the background reads (an account read at most once a minute, a local scan every 3 seconds while indexing and every 30 once complete), so the first request after serve starts shows sources still indexing.
A bad Codex home setting stops `evie serve` at startup: more than four EVIE_CODEX_HOMES entries, or a relative path there or in CODEX_HOME, is fatal there although usage is only a diagnostic view.

Account totals and local detail overlap and are never added together; local records carry no account, and Evie's source leaves out compaction, extraction and unrecorded failed calls and names requested, not billed, models.
The account source's label carries the signed-in Codex email, which reaches the browser as an account label; credentials and raw subprocess errors do not.

summary.text: The finance command: a thin CLI over internal/finance that links banks through Plaid Hosted Link, syncs transactions, seeds categorization rules, categorizes, and opens the database.

does.text: link runs the shared, durable Hosted Link flow: it prints the hosted URL, then polls until the bank is linked, expired, cancelled or failed, giving up after 35 minutes.
sync syncs every linked bank and prints each bank's counts, warnings and failures, then the totals, and exits non-zero when any bank failed.
rules seeds merchant rules from ~/.finance/merchantLookup.json and then the built-in name rules embedded in internal/finance.
categorize mints Budget Entries for posted transactions that have none, and prints how many were categorized and how many remain uncategorized.
db opens the database, which applies the schema, and prints that it is ok.

owns.text: Nothing of its own: every command reads and writes internal/finance's database at ~/.finance/finance.db.

interfaces.text: Subcommands link, sync, rules, categorize, db and help; a missing or unknown command prints the usage to stderr and exits 2.
Plaid credentials come from PLAID_CLIENT_ID and PLAID_SECRET in the environment, read by internal/finance against Plaid's production environment.

gotchas.text: main calls godotenv.Load("../../.env", ".env"), which stops at the first missing file, so .env is never read when ../../.env is absent, although the comment calls it a fallback; evie loads each file in a separate call for this reason, and also reads ~/.evie/.env, which finance never does.
categorize.spec.md also specifies finance review, finance set and rules list or add; none of those subcommands exists, and rules only seeds from the fixed merchantLookup.json path.
db checks nothing beyond opening the file, and its message names only the items and transactions tables whatever else the schema holds.

The CLI shares ~/.finance/finance.db with evie serve; a unique index on finance_link_sessions allows one pending or exchanging link across both processes, so a CLI link picks up a pending flow the web started instead of starting another.

summary.text: The ytscribe command: the CLI for Evie's YouTube transcript library, with fetch, scrape, import and help, owning all printing.

does.text: fetch prints one video's metadata and full transcript, saying whether it came from the cache or the network, with --language (default en) and --refresh.

scrape walks a channel's videos serially, the whole channel when --limit is 0 (the default), printing one progress line per video and a summary, with --delay between network attempts (1.5 seconds by default).
import copies a legacy transcript corpus from a root folder and prints counts of seen, inserted, updated, skipped, matched, unmatched, failed and warnings.

owns.text: Nothing of its own: it opens the transcript library's writable database through internal/youtube for each command.

interfaces.text: Exit codes: 2 for bad usage, 1 for a failed fetch or for any per-item failure in scrape or import, 0 otherwise.
The package variables openYTScribeDB, newYTScribeService and importYTScribeLegacy are its test seams.

gotchas.text: scrape with no limit walks a channel's full history, whereas the youtube_scrape_channel chat tool examines 1 to 50 newest videos, 10 by default.
Flag errors print only the usage text, because each flag set's own output is discarded.
It writes the same transcripts database the Evie tools write, opened writable with the schema applied.

summary.text: Owns MCP Connections: the record of each hosted MCP server, the OAuth sign-in that connects it, the Keychain that holds its credentials, the HTTP transport that carries its tokens, and the pool of live MCP sessions.

does.text: Adds a connection after validating its name (1 to 24 lowercase letters, digits or dashes, starting with a letter) and its https URL, recording it as not_connected under the Connection ID mcp-<name>.
Saves a pre-registered client's secret straight to the Keychain when the connection is added, before the record is created.

Starts a sign-in by discovering the server's protected-resource metadata (from a 401's resource_metadata, else the well-known paths) and its authorization server's metadata, refusing a server without PKCE S256 or with non-https endpoints.
Settles the OAuth client: the pre-registered client ID, an earlier dynamic registration while its issuer and redirect URI are unchanged, or a new Dynamic Client Registration as a public client.

Keeps each pending attempt (state, PKCE verifier, client and metadata) in memory for ten minutes and returns an authorization URL carrying the S256 challenge, the resource indicator and any advertised scopes.
Completes the callback once per unexpired state: it exchanges the code with the verifier, saves the tokens to the Keychain, then records status connected with the OAuth metadata.
Hands out each connection's bearer token, refreshing under that connection's lock a minute before expiry or once after a 401, and saving rotated tokens before using them.

Disconnects by revoking the refresh token (or the access token) when the server lists a revocation endpoint, keeping only the client registration in the Keychain, setting not_connected, and then running disconnect hooks such as closing the live session.

Keeps at most one live MCP session per connection, opened on first use with the official SDK over Streamable HTTP, advertising no client capabilities and with multi-round-trip and the standalone SSE stream off.
Lists a server's tools fresh on every request, hashing each tool's name, description, input schema and annotations as sorted-key JSON into its reviewed selector <name>@<sha256>.
Sends one tools/call per request and shapes the answer: text joined, structuredContent appended as JSON, and images, audio and resources as one-line placeholders.

owns.text: The Connection record type, which never carries credentials; eviedb persists it in mcp_connections through the Records interface declared here.

One Keychain generic-password item per connection, with service dev.evie.mcp and the Connection ID as account, holding the access and refresh tokens, expiry, client ID and client secret as JSON of at most 3,000 bytes.
The serve process's in-memory sign-in state: pending attempts keyed by state, and per connection a credential cache, its lock, and rotated credentials the Keychain has not accepted yet.
The live MCP sessions, one entry per connection in the pool's map.

interfaces.text: Manager offers List, Connection, Add, BeginConnect, Callback, Wait and Disconnect to the owner's surfaces; web's MCPConnections interface names the six its routes use.
It consumes Records (implemented by eviedb's Store) and Secrets (implemented by Keychain), wired by serve's composition.
TokenSource (Token, and Refresh with the rejected token) is what the transport needs; NewHTTPClient builds a connection's client on Evie's transport, with no redirect following.
Pool offers ListTools, CallTool, Close and CloseAll, and satisfies mcpchat's Tools interface.
A failed call comes back as a CallError whose outcome, from SendTrace, is not_sent, rejected or unknown.
Keychain runs /usr/bin/security through an injectable SecurityRunner, so tests capture argv and stdin.

gotchas.text: Only evie serve builds a Manager, so exactly one process holds and refreshes tokens; the evie connections commands are thin clients of serve's routes and fail when serve is not running.
The code exchange and every refresh run detached from the caller's context with a 30-second limit, so a cancelled turn cannot lose a refresh token the server already rotated.
When the Keychain refuses rotated tokens they stay in memory marked unsaved and unused, and the next token request retries the save first.

Only an OAuth refusal (invalid_grant, invalid_client or unauthorized_client on a 400 or 401) sets needs_sign_in and drops the tokens; any other refresh failure sets unreachable and keeps the refresh token.
Secret material reaches security(1) only on stdin, as quoted base64 in a `security -i` line, never in argv.

The transport adds the bearer only over https to the connection's own host, re-sends exactly once after a 401 answered by a successful refresh, refuses redirects, and clears GetBody so net/http cannot replay a POST.
A server's JSON-RPC error is a complete answer (rejected) and keeps the shared session; only a broken connection drops it, and a caller's own cancellation or timeout does not.
No lock is held across network work: Close forgets a session and closes it in the background, and a session that finishes opening after a disconnect is closed and reported as disconnected.
A tool listing stops silently at 500 tools per server.
The redirect URI is built from EVIE_ADDR, and a dynamic registration is reused only while that URI and the issuer still match, so changing EVIE_ADDR means a new registration at the next connect.
A used attempt stays in memory until it expires, and Wait keeps waiting for a callback that has already started, even past the deadline.

summary.text: A fake hosted MCP endpoint and OAuth authorization server for tests, shaped like Square's: a 401 with resource_metadata, Dynamic Client Registration for public clients, PKCE S256, and a rotated refresh token on every refresh.

does.text: Runs one TLS httptest server whose /mcp answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL unless the bearer is a token it issued, and serves protected-resource and authorization-server metadata.
Registers clients that ask for exactly one redirect URI and token_endpoint_auth_method none, issuing client IDs dcr-1, dcr-2 and so on.
Approve plays the owner signing in: it checks the authorization URL's parameters, including S256 and the resource, and returns the code and state the browser would carry to Evie's callback.
Checks a code exchange against the stored client, redirect URI, PKCE challenge and resource, and on each refresh issues new tokens and retires the old refresh token.
Can be switched to refuse registration, fail every refresh with invalid_grant, answer refreshes with any status and body, or run a hook between rotation and the answer.

owns.text: Only in-memory test state: issued codes, live tokens, and a Snapshot of registrations, refreshes, token forms, revoked tokens and the Authorization headers its MCP endpoint saw.

interfaces.text: NewAuthServer(t), Resource, Approve, Snapshot and the Set switches; mcpconn's manager tests and eviedb's secret-leak test use it.

gotchas.text: Its /mcp endpoint is not an MCP server: with a valid token it answers an empty JSON-RPC result to anything, so tests that list or call tools stand up the SDK's real Streamable HTTP server instead.
Its metadata lists both plain and S256 challenge methods and client_secret_basic, client_secret_post and none, so Evie's own choices decide what is sent.
It is a non-test package so that eviedb's leak test can run against the real SQLite file; the facts mark it as test support by its name.
Revocation records any token it is sent and only forgets it when it is a live refresh token.

summary.text: The Workspace side of MCP connections: decides which reviewed server tools a chat may reach, and applies the owner's tool review and Tool Policies to Workspace Access.

does.text: Computes a chat's reach: per mcp- Connection ID, the reviewed selectors present both in the Workspace Access revision the chat pinned at creation and in the current access; a chat with no pin reaches nothing.
Reviews a connection's live tools for one Workspace as enabled, changed (an older hash is reviewed), available or unselectable, plus the reviewed names the server no longer offers.
Enables a tool by replacing any older reviewed version with <name>@<hash>; the first enabled tool attaches the connection to the Workspace and disabling the last one removes it.
Writes each access change expecting the revision it read, so a concurrent change is refused and nothing is written.
Sets Allow or Ask on the current version of an enabled tool, and answers whether a selector is allowed in the latest policy revision.
Passes Connection, ListTools and CallTool through to the record store and the pool, so one Service meets the mcp plugin's MCPChat interface.

owns.text: No storage of its own: reviewed tools are Workspace Access resources under the Connection ID, and Tool Policies are eviedb's workspace_mcp_tool_policies revisions, both reached through its Store interface.
The one definition of a reviewed tool's standing (ToolState) and of a Tool Policy (ask or allow), shared by the chat tools and the review routes.

interfaces.text: Service offers Reach, Connection, ListTools, CallTool, Allowed, Review, SetToolEnabled and SetToolPolicy; web's MCPToolReview names the last three.
It consumes Store, the access and policy state eviedb implements, and Tools, the server reach mcpconn's Pool implements.
SelectableName says whether a server tool's name may be enabled.

gotchas.text: Disabling works without the server: a failed listing leaves the tools unknown and the review marked Unlisted with the reviewed names, so revoking never waits for a sign-in.
Disabling is two writes, the access change and then clearing Allow on every version of that tool, each with its own expected revision; if the second fails the access is already revoked.
SelectableName measures len(name), so its 64 limit counts bytes, while the spec says characters.
Review and SetToolPolicy list the server's tools, so both need the connection signed in and reachable.
Reach is an error, not an empty answer, when the chat's pin names a different Workspace from the one asked about.
Chats created before access pins existed have no pin and so reach no MCP tools.

summary.text: The small GitHub REST client the Changes feature reads and writes through, with one fine-grained token sent only in the Authorization header.

does.text: Reads the token's user, which proves the token works, one repository, and the token owner's own repositories, newest first.
Creates a repository on the token owner's personal account, optionally with GitHub's first commit so it can be cloned.
Lists open pull requests and the pull requests on one head branch in any state, and reads one pull request with its merged and mergeable fields.
Reads a commit's checks as GitHub Actions workflow runs and commit statuses, because GitHub's Checks API does not accept fine-grained tokens.
Opens a ready (not draft) pull request, merges one with Rebase and merge only while its head is the expected SHA, and closes one without merging.

Maps GitHub's answers to typed errors: 401 unauthorized, 404 not found or invisible, 403 forbidden, 422 refused, 405 not mergeable and 409 head changed, carrying GitHub's own explanation cut to 200 bytes.

owns.text: No state beyond its API base, token and HTTP client; the repositories and pull requests live on GitHub, and the changes sync records what it reads through eviedb.

interfaces.text: Client and its methods; changes declares the slices it consumes as GitHubClient, PullRequestClient, PullRequestOpener and PullRequestMerger.
New takes the API base so tests point it at a fake server; API is the production base.
ValidName and the invalid-name, number, SHA and ref errors are checked before any request is made.

gotchas.text: Every list is one page of at most 100 with no pagination; sync makes up for pull requests past the first page by reading each one it last saw open.
GitHub answers 404 both for a missing repository and for one the token cannot see, so callers word it as an access problem.
The token is GITHUB_TOKEN, read by startup composition; without it no client is built and GitHub actions are refused with ErrNoToken.
A transport failure names only the host and unwraps the URL error, so no request URL reaches an error message.
The default HTTP client times out after ten seconds, and a response is read up to 8 MB.

summary.text: Owns the personal-finance domain: linking banks through Plaid Hosted Link, syncing transactions into ~/.finance/finance.db, rule-based categorization into Budget Entries, the review workflow's read and write, and the Spending views' queries.

does.text: Opens the one database at ~/.finance/finance.db, applying the whole schema on every writable open and locking the file to 0600 because Plaid access tokens live in it.
Links a bank through Plaid Hosted Link as a durable flow, at most one pending at a time, and saves the exchanged access token with the item.

Syncs every linked bank through /transactions/sync, committing each page with its cursor in one SQL transaction; one bank's failure does not stop the others, and a mutation-during-pagination error is retried once from the committed cursor.
Deletes a removed transaction's budget entries before the transaction itself, so a retracted pending row cannot wedge a bank's sync.

Categorizes every posted transaction without a Budget Entry: the legacy category column first, then an exact case-insensitive merchant rule, then the lowest-priority matching name rule, with disagreement at equal priority an error.
Seeds merchant rules from a JSON file and name rules from an embedded, owner-reviewed seed, both as upserts.

Performs the workflow effects sync_ledger, categorize_ledger and apply_review once per idempotency key, recording an effect receipt so a replay returns the recorded output and reconciliation answers from it.
Builds review batches of transactions awaiting review with deterministic evidence, and applies the owner's answered batch through the same rechecks Categorize uses.
Serves the Spending views: the yearly daily flow, monthly cash flow, transactions by classification, one day's detail, a single category edit, a refresh, and the connected-account inventory.

owns.text: The finance database's tables: items, transactions, categories, rules, name_rules, budget_entries, budget_limits, review_decisions and effect_receipts, plus finance_accounts, finance_account_snapshots and finance_link_sessions.
Each linked bank's Plaid access token and sync cursor, in items.
The categories excluded and Credit Card Payments, whose entries count toward no Overview figure.

interfaces.text: Package functions shared by the CLI and the agent (OpenDB, Link, Sync, Categorize, the seeders, the effects and the review functions) return data rather than printing, with Link the exception.
SpendingService backs the web Spending and account routes, whose SpendingService and SpendingAccountsService interfaces name what they use.
Plaid access uses PLAID_CLIENT_ID and PLAID_SECRET against Plaid's production environment; there is no sandbox mode.

gotchas.text: Plaid access tokens sit in plain text in finance.db (mode 0600); MCP's tokens went to the Keychain partly to avoid this, and moving Plaid there is a stated non-goal.
Pending transactions never get a Budget Entry (the Pending Fence): Plaid replaces them with posted rows, and an entry at the pending amount would be wrong.
The schema is CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, applied on every writable open; there is no migration step.
The sync gate is a channel inside one process, so the finance CLI and evie serve are not serialized against each other; each page still commits atomically with its cursor.

categorize.spec.md describes categorizing through the reviewed and category_source columns, but the code mints budget_entries for posted transactions that have none and no longer writes the legacy category column.
sync_ledger records its receipt only after the last bank, so an interrupted sync leaves none although some pages committed; a re-sent intent continues from the committed cursor.
Spend queries that sum across all categories must leave out excluded and Credit Card Payments.
A category edit opens an existing database only, so it can never create the file or apply the schema.

summary.text: Owns Evie's durable YouTube transcript library: its database, the HTTP protocol that reads YouTube, cache-first fetch and channel scrape, and the legacy corpus import.

does.text: Fetches one video's transcript cache-first: a cached transcript, or a cached terminal outcome, is returned without touching YouTube unless refresh is set.
Reads YouTube by fetching the watch page for its API key, asking the youtubei player endpoint as the Android client, and downloading the chosen caption track as json3.
Saves the channel, video, transcript and ready state together, and records terminal outcomes (no captions, language unavailable, unavailable) so later fetches skip them.
Scrapes a channel serially: lists its newest videos (all of them when the limit is zero), saves the listing, skips cached transcripts and terminal outcomes, and waits between network attempts.
Imports a legacy file corpus by copying transcript files, never moving or editing them.
Indexes transcripts in an FTS5 table kept current by triggers, and offers a transcript_library view that prefers a manual transcript over a generated one over a legacy one.

owns.text: The transcript database at ~/.evie/transcripts/transcripts.db (folder 0700, file 0600): channels, videos, transcripts, transcript_states, the transcript_library view and the transcript_fts index.

interfaces.text: OpenDB, OpenDBReadOnly and OpenDBAt; NewClient and NewService with Fetch and Scrape; and ImportLegacy.
The youtube_transcript and youtube_scrape_channel tools and ytscribe are thin adapters, and query_db reads the library through the read-only opener.

gotchas.text: The protocol uses YouTube's internal youtubei player endpoint posing as Android client 20.10.38, not a public API.
A request is tried at most three times, retrying only on 429 or 5xx with Retry-After honored up to 30 seconds; consent, reCAPTCHA and bot-confirmation pages fail at once.
Responses are capped at 10 MiB, and the default client times out after 30 seconds.
Caption URLs and their redirects are validated before they are followed.
A refresh that fails keeps the existing transcript and its ready state.
The schema is one idempotent blob applied on every writable open, with no migration framework.

summary.text: A Workspace's Repository and the Changes made in it: detection, creation and publishing, the merged list of Evie's build branches and GitHub pull requests, sync, push, merge, close and cleanup.

does.text: Reads the Repository from the Workspace folder every time, never storing it: none, local (a non-bare work tree's top level), or GitHub when origin names github.com/<owner>/<name> in HTTPS, SSH or scp-like form.
For a GitHub Repository it checks the token against GitHub, takes GitHub's default branch as the base, and counts how many commits the local base branch is behind origin's.

Sets up a new Workspace's Repository before the Workspace is registered: a new local repository on main with one empty commit, a new GitHub repository cloned into the folder, or an existing one cloned or adopted when its origin matches.
Publishes a local Repository: creates the GitHub repository, sets origin, and pushes only the base branch; publishing again with the same name retries the push.

Lists Changes by merging Evie's build branches, read from build attempts, with the synced pull requests, linking a pull request to the build on its branch and keeping the 20 most recent finished ones.
Syncs each GitHub Repository every 60 seconds while serve runs, one sync per Workspace at a time: open pull requests, the checks on each head, and pull requests that left the open list.
Pushes one of Evie's draft branches over HTTPS, after running the Workspace's Verify command when one is set, then opens or finds its pull request into the base the Change was built from.

Merges for the owner (a local Change through the Kernel's merge gate, a GitHub Change by Rebase and merge of the head Evie last showed), and arms or disarms Merge when checks pass, which each sync then fires.
After a merge or close it deletes Evie's own branch on GitHub and locally, removes its worktree, and fast-forwards the owner's base branch only when it is checked out with no uncommitted edits.
Shows one Change with its diff through localfiles.Compare, fetching a pull request into refs/evie/pull/<number> when no branch of Evie's holds it.

owns.text: The Change model (draft, open, merged and closed states; checks; the armed and needs-rebase markers) shared by the web routes and the CLI.
No tables of its own: Evie's Changes are derived from build attempts, while synced pull requests, merge arms and Change notices are stored by eviedb through interfaces declared here.
The in-process folder claim that lets one action at a time change a Repository, and the per-Workspace sync claim.

interfaces.text: Service (Repository, Prepare, Publish, GitHubRepositories, Account), Lister (List, Show), Syncer (Run, Sync, Refresh), Pusher (Push, PushForWorkflow, FindPullRequest) and Merger (Merge, Close, Arm, Disarm, AfterSync).

It consumes GitHubClient, PullRequestClient, PullRequestOpener and PullRequestMerger for GitHub, BuildGate for the Kernel's merge gate, Verifier for Verify, and Source, BuildRecords, PullRequestRecords, PullRequestStore, MergeRecords and MergeArms for storage.
Repository.Resource names a GitHub Repository to workflows as repo:<owner>/<name>, the resource a workflow's push must name.

gotchas.text: The spec's Change model says Changes are stored per Workspace with their state and markers, but nothing is stored for Evie's builds: their state is derived from each build attempt's gate and worktree, and only pull requests are stored.
The token reaches git only as an http.extraheader in a per-command environment, with credential helpers and every protocol but HTTPS off, and it is scrubbed from error text.
A merge's own sync cannot run AfterSync on the folder the merge still holds, so a merge cleans up and catches up by itself; AfterSync skips a busy folder until the next sync.
The folder claim is a map inside one Service, so it serializes actions within one process only; evie changes merge builds its own Merger in the CLI process.
A GitHub merge is refused when the pull request has new commits since Evie last read it, is a GitHub draft, or is reported unmergeable; a conflict is recorded against that head as needs rebase.

Merge when checks pass needs at least one check, merges once every check passed or was neutral or skipped, clears on a failed check or a conflict, and stays set across new commits and errors that may pass.
A sync that GitHub refuses records nothing, so a missing check is never read as no checks.
A workflow's push needs Verify set and passing, while the owner's push goes ahead after a failed Verify and the pull request body says so.
Opening a pull request that fails without GitHub refusing it is ErrOpenUncertain: the pull request may exist, and pushing again finds it.
Cleanup deletes a branch only when the Change is Evie's and the branch starts with evie/; the owner's branches are never deleted.

summary.text: Owns the lifecycle of a build worker's git worktree as the harness: plan it, create it on a fresh evie/ branch, commit the worker's changes, report the branch, run the merge gate's rebase and fast-forward, and clean it up.

does.text: Plans without changing anything: the folder must be a non-bare repository's top level with no merge, rebase or similar in progress, the base (by default the checked-out branch) is pinned to a commit, and the branch is evie/<id prefix>-<slug of the objective>.
Places a worktree at <repo>/.evie/worktrees/<attempt> with a private temp folder at <repo>/.evie/tmp/<attempt>, and adds /.evie/ to the repository's local info/exclude, never to a tracked file.
Creates the worktree on its branch from the pinned base commit, or proves an existing one is a plain folder linked to its pinned git directory and on its branch.
Commits every change as the harness, with the repository's identity or Evie's when none is set and no hooks, and refuses a worktree that holds a nested .git.
Reports a branch against its base: its head, up to 50 commits, the files changed with line counts, and whether uncommitted changes remain.
Rebases a branch inside its worktree, and on a conflict aborts so the branch stays as it was and reports the conflicting files.

Fast-forwards a merge target with git merge --ff-only in the checkout that has it, which refuses to overwrite uncommitted changes, and otherwise by a compare-and-swap of the ref; it never merges into a build worktree and never pushes.
Removes a worktree and its temp folder, and its branch when asked, pruning a worktree that is already gone.
Proposes setup and verify commands found in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, as a suggestion only, for Workspace creation and the Verify settings; the owner sets the commands.

owns.text: The .evie/worktrees and .evie/tmp folders inside a repository and the evie/ branches it creates; the Worktree record is delegation's type, persisted by its callers.

interfaces.text: Plan, Ensure, Commit and Report run a build worker's worktree for subagents; Status and Remove also back the evie worktrees command; Exists checks that a worktree folder is present.

Compares two revisions for a Change (base...head, renames found): each file's status, line counts, ending blob and hunks, reading patches for at most 100 files and withholding excluded files such as .env.
